{"concept_id":"drv.motion.left_turn","kind":"formula","contract":"The road user has turned to the left: counting from the onset of the turning — the observation at which its rate of change of heading to the left first rose above the onset yaw rate, a rate the caller sets — the heading change accumulated since that onset reaches at least the turn angle, a size the caller sets, to the left. {"node_id":"NRS_484A_450_2","law_refs":["NRS-484A-450-2"],"subject":{"binder":"v","class_elements":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"]},"segmentation":[{"id":"s1","text":"Every driver of a vehicle","role":"subject"},{"id":"s2","text":"approaching a stop intersection indicated by a stop sign","role":"trigger"},{"id":"s3","text":"shall stop before entering the crosswalk on the near side of the intersection or, if there is no crosswalk, shall stop at a clearly marked stop line, or if none, then at the point nearest the intersecting highway","role":"obligation"},{"id":"s4","text":"where the driver has a view of approaching traffic on the intersecting highway","role":"standard"},{"id":"s5","text":"before entering the intersection.","role":"condition"}],"elements":[{"span":"s1","atoms":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"],"derived":[],"justification":"“vehicle” is the term DEF-NRS-484A-320 defines and the run admits as the aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, so the span claims ru.aggregate with that id: the atom is “membership of a legal aggregate: the atom's literal argument is an aggregate id”, true where the road user carries an included class, unknown where an included or unresolved class it might carry is unobserved. Its exclusion “not a stand-in for a named road-user class” does not apply, because the admitted aggregate is claimed as the aggregate and never replaced by a class atom; its exclusion of “a relational role such as who drives or controls a vehicle” is respected by reading “driver” through the vehicle's controlled motion (narrowing on this span) rather than as a member of the aggregate."},{"span":"s2","atoms":["st.intersection","st.travel_region","rel.occupies","st.lane_enters","dev.stop_sign","dev.governs"],"derived":[],"justification":"The approach is read as the ontology's section on an act due at a place before an event states it: “a road user's approach to an intersection is a carrier it occupies (rel.occupies) whose entrance end is that intersection”. st.intersection is “the region where two roadways meet, bounded by the prolongation of their edges”, the region the words call the intersection; The second place is st.stop_line, “the transverse line marking where vehicles halt for a device”, taken where the crosswalk's observed list of entrances excludes the carrier, as st.entrance_of's completeness clause permits. The third is the point nearest the intersecting highway, read on the carrier (st.travel_region) against the way the junction lies on: st.highway is “the entire width between the boundary lines of every way”, st.on_way “the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on — … an intersection lies on every way that meets there”, so the intersecting highway is a way the intersection lies on other than the one the carrier lies on. the primitive's own inputs are not claimed again beyond st.lane_direction and st.region_geometry, which the rule also reads on their own for the direction and for the distance, since prim.region_offset_along “is a geometric quantity only … a distance to the region is read from st.region_geometry, never from this value”. rel.occupies excludes a halt whose footprint already overlaps the crossing or the junction, which the words place the halt before, and st.intersection is the region that entry concerns."},{"span":"s5","atoms":["st.intersection","rel.occupies"],"derived":[],"justification":"“before entering the intersection” is the event the duty is owed before: the observation at which the vehicle's footprint first overlaps the intersection region. rel.occupies is “a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region (… intersection …)” and st.intersection the region itself; st.intersection's exclusion “not a stand-in for a crosswalk or a stop line — a stop before the crossing is earlier than a stop before the intersection” is precisely the distinction kept here, the crossing being the place of the act in s3 and the junction the event in this span."}],"operationalizations":[{"span":"s4","standard":"where the driver has a view of approaching traffic on the intersecting highway","concepts":["st.sight_along_way","st.highway","st.on_way","st.intersection","rel.visible","ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic","st.travel_region","rel.occupies"],"params":["p.intersecting_way_view_distance"],"convention":"Intersection sight-distance convention (AASHTO Green Book intersection sight distance, the departure-sight-triangle cases): a driver halted at the stopping point must be able to see along the major way at least the distance an approaching vehicle travels in the time needed to judge a gap and clear the junction. Where the sign's governance of the carrier is unobserved, whether the rule applies is unknown; where the source's complete record shows the sign governs no carrier the vehicle occupies, the rule does not apply.","obligation":"At each observation at which the vehicle's footprint first overlaps the intersection it approaches (the entry event: the rise of rel.occupies of the vehicle on the intersection X that the carrier it occupies runs into, st.lane_enters, read from this observation and the one before it), the vehicle must have been at a standstill (drv.motion.standstill with p.standstill_speed_tolerance) at some observation of the approach that leads to that entry, with its body at the place the words name. The place is read from the words in their order: first the crosswalk that marks the entrance of the carrier the vehicle approaches through (st.entrance_of on the same carrier st.lane_enters relates to X); where that crosswalk's entrances are observed, so that its list is complete, and exclude the carrier, the clearly marked stop line that marks it; where neither marks it, the point on the carrier nearest the intersecting highway at which the view of s4 is met. Where a mark's association with the carrier is not observed, whether that mark governs is unknown and the duty is unknown on that ground. A halt counts at the place where the distance from the vehicle's body to the mark (st.region_geometry) is within p.stop_point_tolerance and the mark lies ahead along the carrier's designated direction (the sign of prim.region_offset_along with st.lane_direction); the words placing the halt before the vehicle enters the crossing and the junction, a halt at which its footprint already overlaps that region (rel.occupies) is not at the place, and the tolerance applies outside that region only. The search for the halt runs back from the entry event and ends only at the start of that approach — the last observation before the event at which the vehicle, on a carrier the mark marks, is off the mark, short of it and farther from it than p.stop_point_tolerance — or at the previous entry of the same vehicle into the same intersection; nothing else ends it: not another junction or mark, not the start of the recording, not a first observation, not a distance travelled. Only an observed exit from the stopping zone upstream begins a new approach, so a vehicle that leaves the zone upstream and returns owes the halt again, while crossing the mark, moving on toward the junction, a change of carrier, a lateral move or a reverse within the zone begin none and lose no halt already made. Where the search finds the halt the duty is met; where it reaches either end without the halt the duty is violated; where it reaches neither end without finding it — the recording begins inside the stopping zone, the observation before the event does not show the vehicle's place relative to the mark through its carrier, or the speed that decides the standstill is unobserved — the duty is unknown. {"concept_id":"drv.motion.left_turn","kind":"formula","contract":"The road user has turned to the left: counting from the onset of the turning — the observation at which its rate of change of heading to the left first rose above the onset yaw rate, a rate the caller sets — the heading change accumulated since that onset reaches at least the turn angle, a size the caller sets, to the left. The concept becomes true at the observation at which that angle is first reached and stays true at the later observations at which the accumulated change still holds it, until a later onset starts the count again; the integration is bounded by the heading step, the largest interval between consecutive observations it may integrate across. It states the turning of the body only: no place, no lane, no way and no destination. Not a stand-in for: a signal or a declared intention, a steering input, the curvature of the road — a body yaws on a straight road whenever it manoeuvres — a lane change, or a reversal of the direction of travel, which is a larger angle and has its own concept.","definition":null,"args":[{"name":"u","sort":"track"}],"params":[{"name":"heading_step","unit":"ms","meaning":"the largest interval between two consecutive observations the heading integration may cross, the sampling standard of the acquisition profile"},{"name":"onset_yaw_rate","unit":"deg/s","meaning":"the rate of change of heading above which the body is read as beginning to turn rather than running straight, which fixes the observed onset the heading change is counted from"},{"name":"turn_angle","unit":"deg","meaning":"the accumulated heading change at which a turn to the left is recognized"}],"act":{"boundary":"event","onset":"the observation at which its rate of change of heading to the left first rose above the onset yaw rate","recognition":"the observation at which the heading change accumulated since that onset reaches at least the turn angle","extent":"the later observations at which the accumulated change still holds the turn angle, until a later onset starts the count again","history":"the onset must be observed, with the rate of change of heading known at every observation from the one before it onwards and no interval between consecutive observations longer than the heading step; {"concept_id":"drv.motion.u_turn","kind":"formula","contract":"The road user's direction of travel upon a way has reversed: counting from the onset of the manoeuvre — the observation at which the magnitude of its rate of change of heading first rose above the onset yaw rate, a rate the caller sets — the magnitude of the heading change accumulated since that onset reaches at least the reversal angle, a size the caller sets below a half turn, while the road user's footprint overlaps a way. The definition this contract carries is the turning of a vehicle upon a highway “so as to proceed in the opposite direction”, “whether accomplished by one continuous movement or not”, so halts, rearward movements and steering the other way between the onset and the reversal do not end the manoeuvre, and the count runs on until the angle is reached or a later onset starts it again; the integration is bounded by the heading step, the largest interval between consecutive observations it may integrate across. The reversal angle is the contract's own magnitude, the bound within which a sampled heading change is read as the opposite direction. Not a stand-in for: a turn through a smaller angle, which has its own concept, a turn into another way, travel against a designated direction of travel, a reversing movement, or a signal or a declared intention.","definition":"DEF-NRS-484B-077","args":[{"name":"u","sort":"track"}],"params":[{"name":"heading_step","unit":"ms","meaning":"the largest interval between two consecutive observations the heading integration may cross, the sampling standard of the acquisition profile"},{"name":"onset_yaw_rate","unit":"deg/s","meaning":"the rate of change of heading above which the body is read as beginning to turn rather than running straight, which fixes the observed onset the heading change is counted from"},{"name":"reversal_angle","unit":"deg","meaning":"the accumulated heading change at which the definition's proceeding in the opposite direction is recognized; lines: -{"node_id":"NRS_484A_450_2","law_refs":["NRS-484A-450-2"],"subject":{"binder":"v","class_elements":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"]},"segmentation":[{"id":"s1","text":"Every driver of a vehicle","role":"subject"},{"id":"s2","text":"approaching a stop intersection indicated by a stop sign","role":"trigger"},{"id":"s3","text":"shall stop before entering the crosswalk on the near side of the intersection or, if there is no crosswalk, shall stop at a clearly marked stop line, or if none, then at the point nearest the intersecting highway","role":"obligation"},{"id":"s4","text":"where the driver has a view of approaching traffic on the intersecting highway","role":"standard"},{"id":"s5","text":"before entering the intersection.","role":"condition"}],"elements":[{"span":"s1","atoms":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"],"derived":[],"justification":"“vehicle” is the term DEF-NRS-484A-320 defines and the run admits as the aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, so the span claims ru.aggregate with that id: the atom is “membership of a legal aggregate: the atom's literal argument is an aggregate id”, true where the road user carries an included class, unknown where an included or unresolved class it might carry is unobserved. Its exclusion “not a stand-in for a named road-user class” does not apply, because the admitted aggregate is claimed as the aggregate and never replaced by a class atom; its exclusion of “a relational role such as who drives or controls a vehicle” is respected by reading “driver” through the vehicle's controlled motion (narrowing on this span) rather than as a member of the aggregate."},{"span":"s2","atoms":["st.intersection","st.travel_region","rel.occupies","st.lane_enters","dev.stop_sign","dev.governs"],"derived":[],"justification":"The approach is read as the ontology's section on an act due at a place before an event states it: “a road user's approach to an intersection is a carrier it occupies (rel.occupies) whose entrance end is that intersection”. st.intersection is “the region where two roadways meet, bounded by the prolongation of their edges”, the region the words call the intersection; st.travel_region is the kind the carrier quantifier ranges over, “the union of the kinds a device can govern … a lane and the kinds that refine it, a bicycle lane or path, a roadway and the kinds that refine it, a shoulder, or an intersection”, which is exactly the set of carriers st.lane_enters admits, so each region argument of the claimed relations has a claimed kind; st.lane_enters is “the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end”, and its clause “it is entry topology: it is decided where the source records it … never inferred from distance, overlap or a road user's velocity” is why approaching is not read from heading or closing speed. dev.stop_sign is the “regulatory sign requiring a full halt”, the sign the words name, and dev.governs, “the travel regions whose traffic the device controls … or an intersection”, ties it to the carrier the vehicle approaches through, as the ontology directs (“the mark that governs that approach is one the source records as marking that carrier”); dev.governs's exclusion “not a stand-in for a position” does not apply, because the place of the halt is read from the crosswalk, the stop line or the view point in s3 and never from where the sign stands. rel.occupies is “a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region”, the anchor that makes the carrier the subject's own."},{"span":"s3","atoms":["st.crosswalk","st.stop_line","st.travel_region","st.entrance_of","st.lane_direction","st.region_geometry","rel.occupies","st.intersection","st.highway","st.on_way","prim.region_offset_along"],"derived":["drv.motion.standstill"],"justification":"“shall stop” is the act: drv.motion.standstill carries the posted definition DEF-NRS-484A-255, “complete cessation from movement”, as a motion state at an observation, with the speed tolerance the sampling leaves to the observer. The first place is the crosswalk “on the near side of the intersection”: st.crosswalk is the “marked crossing, or the unmarked prolongation of sidewalks at an intersection”, and which crossing is the near one is st.entrance_of, “the carrier whose entrance into an intersection a stop line or a crosswalk marks — exactly that carrier's entrance, the line or crossing a vehicle approaching through that carrier halts at or before”, read on the same carrier st.lane_enters relates to the intersection; st.entrance_of's exclusion “not a stand-in for distance to the line” is why nearness never selects the crossing. The second place is st.stop_line, “the transverse line marking where vehicles halt for a device”, taken where the crosswalk's observed list of entrances excludes the carrier, as st.entrance_of's completeness clause permits. The third is the point nearest the intersecting highway, read on the carrier (st.travel_region) against the way the junction lies on: st.highway is “the entire width between the boundary lines of every way”, st.on_way “the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on — … an intersection lies on every way that meets there”, so the intersecting highway is a way the intersection lies on other than the one the carrier lies on. That the halt is at the place and on the near side of it is st.region_geometry, “the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it”, within p.stop_point_tolerance, with the side taken from prim.region_offset_along, “the signed distance … measured along a carrier's designated direction (st.lane_direction)”, whose sign gives the side as the ontology requires (“the side of the mark is read along that carrier's designated direction … never along the road user's heading”); the primitive's own inputs are not claimed again beyond st.lane_direction and st.region_geometry, which the rule also reads on their own for the direction and for the distance, since prim.region_offset_along “is a geometric quantity only … a distance to the region is read from st.region_geometry, never from this value”. rel.occupies excludes a halt whose footprint already overlaps the crossing or the junction, which the words place the halt before, and st.intersection is the region that entry concerns."},{"span":"s5","atoms":["st.intersection","rel.occupies"],"derived":[],"justification":"“before entering the intersection” is the event the duty is owed before: the observation at which the vehicle's footprint first overlaps the intersection region. rel.occupies is “a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region (… intersection …)” and st.intersection the region itself; st.intersection's exclusion “not a stand-in for a crosswalk or a stop line — a stop before the crossing is earlier than a stop before the intersection” is precisely the distinction kept here, the crossing being the place of the act in s3 and the junction the event in this span."}],"operationalizations":[{"span":"s4","standard":"where the driver has a view of approaching traffic on the intersecting highway","concepts":["st.sight_along_way","st.highway","st.on_way","st.intersection","rel.visible","ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic","st.travel_region","rel.occupies"],"params":["p.intersecting_way_view_distance"],"convention":"Intersection sight-distance convention (AASHTO Green Book intersection sight distance, the departure-sight-triangle cases): a driver halted at the stopping point must be able to see along the major way at least the distance an approaching vehicle travels in the time needed to judge a gap and clear the junction. The point is adequate where st.sight_along_way, “the distance along a way, in each direction from the point of that way nearest a road user, within which another vehicle on that way could be seen from the road user's eye at the observation … the smaller of the two directions”, taken for the intersecting highway the junction lies on (st.highway with st.on_way and st.intersection), is at least p.intersecting_way_view_distance, and where a road user that is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic is on that way approaching the junction, that road user is visible from the vehicle (rel.visible, “b is visible from a: an unobstructed line of sight”). The aggregate fixes whose approach counts as the traffic to be seen — “pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances … using any highway for purposes of travel” — and the sight atom carries the view itself, since rel.visible “is not a stand-in for … the sight distance of a place” and st.sight_along_way is “not a stand-in for … whether an actual road user is seen”: the two together read the span's words where a road user is present and where none is. p.intersecting_way_view_distance is the only magnitude, and it is the reading's, not the words'.","surrogate":false}],"assumptions":[],"intentions":[],"compositions":[],"residues":[],"binders":[],"applicability":"The bound road user is a vehicle of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle that occupies a travel region whose entrance end is an intersection (st.lane_enters on that carrier) and that a stop sign governs (dev.stop_sign with dev.governs on that same carrier), and that enters that intersection: the stop intersection indicated by a stop sign which it approaches. Where the sign's governance of the carrier is unobserved, whether the rule applies is unknown; where the source's complete record shows the sign governs no carrier the vehicle occupies, the rule does not apply.","obligation":"At each observation at which the vehicle's footprint first overlaps the intersection it approaches (the entry event: the rise of rel.occupies of the vehicle on the intersection X that the carrier it occupies runs into, st.lane_enters, read from this observation and the one before it), the vehicle must have been at a standstill (drv.motion.standstill with p.standstill_speed_tolerance) at some observation of the approach that leads to that entry, with its body at the place the words name. The place is read from the words in their order: first the crosswalk that marks the entrance of the carrier the vehicle approaches through (st.entrance_of on the same carrier st.lane_enters relates to X); where that crosswalk's entrances are observed, so that its list is complete, and exclude the carrier, the clearly marked stop line that marks it; where neither marks it, the point on the carrier nearest the intersecting highway at which the view of s4 is met. Where a mark's association with the carrier is not observed, whether that mark governs is unknown and the duty is unknown on that ground. A halt counts at the place where the distance from the vehicle's body to the mark (st.region_geometry) is within p.stop_point_tolerance and the mark lies ahead along the carrier's designated direction (the sign of prim.region_offset_along with st.lane_direction); the words placing the halt before the vehicle enters the crossing and the junction, a halt at which its footprint already overlaps that region (rel.occupies) is not at the place, and the tolerance applies outside that region only. The search for the halt runs back from the entry event and ends only at the start of that approach — the last observation before the event at which the vehicle, on a carrier the mark marks, is off the mark, short of it and farther from it than p.stop_point_tolerance — or at the previous entry of the same vehicle into the same intersection; nothing else ends it: not another junction or mark, not the start of the recording, not a first observation, not a distance travelled. Only an observed exit from the stopping zone upstream begins a new approach, so a vehicle that leaves the zone upstream and returns owes the halt again, while crossing the mark, moving on toward the junction, a change of carrier, a lateral move or a reverse within the zone begin none and lose no halt already made. Where the search finds the halt the duty is met; where it reaches either end without the halt the duty is violated; where it reaches neither end without finding it — the recording begins inside the stopping zone, the observation before the event does not show the vehicle's place relative to the mark through its carrier, or the speed that decides the standstill is unobserved — the duty is unknown. Each entry owes its own halt: a halt made before the previous entry of the same vehicle into the same intersection discharged that entry, not this one.","params":["p.standstill_speed_tolerance","p.stop_point_tolerance","p.intersecting_way_view_distance"],"narrowings":[{"span":"s1","why":"“Every driver of a vehicle” is read as the vehicle whose motion is controlled. Who or what controls a road user is not observable, and the ontology reads “drives”, “operates” and “the driver” through the vehicle's controlled motion, a vehicle moving on the road being taken to be driven, with the duty binding that vehicle's conduct whoever or whatever is at the controls.","kind":"observable_reading","category":"agency"},{"span":"s2","why":"“indicated by a stop sign” is read as the presence of a stop sign governing the approach. That a sign is official or posted by an authority is a legal status the ontology reads through the feature itself: the sign's presence on the road is the evidence of the designation the section's title speaks of.","kind":"observable_reading","category":"status"},{"span":"s3","why":"“a clearly marked stop line” is read as the stop line the scene represents. The ontology states this reading for exactly these words: the line's presence is the evidence, and the paint's clarity or wear is not modelled. The reading relaxes nothing about which place governs, the act or its timing.","kind":"observable_reading","category":"status"},{"span":"s3","why":"“the point nearest the intersecting highway where the driver has a view” is read as a point on the carrier the vehicle approaches through, rather than any point of the scene: the words single out the vehicle's own approach, and the place is read on the region the node binds. Among the points of that carrier at which the view of s4 is met, the duty is read as met by a halt at or before the nearest such point to the intersecting highway, within p.stop_point_tolerance of it, so a halt farther back on the same carrier that still meets the view is not a violation; this is the reading of “the point nearest … where the driver has a view”, which names a nearest point among those with a view and not a single surveyed spot.","kind":"reading"},{"span":"s4","why":"“the driver has a view of approaching traffic” is read as what could be seen along the intersecting way from where the vehicle stands, and as the visibility of a road user of the traffic aggregate that is there. From the last observation at which the car is off the crossing, short of it and more than the stop-point tolerance from it, through to the observation at which its footprint first overlaps the junction, its speed never falls to the standstill tolerance: it rolls over the crossing at about 4 m/s and enters the junction.","masked":[]},{"name":"permit","expected":"compliant","narrative":"The same approach and the same crossing. {"concept_id":"drv.motion.left_turn","kind":"formula","contract":"The road user has turned to the left: counting from the onset of the turning — the observation at which its rate of change of heading to the left first rose above the onset yaw rate, a rate the caller sets — the heading change accumulated since that onset reaches at least the turn angle, a size the caller sets, to the left. lines: {"node_id":"NRS_484A_450_2","law_refs":["NRS-484A-450-2"],"subject":{"binder":"v","class_elements":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"]},"segmentation":[{"id":"s1","text":"Every driver of a vehicle","role":"subject"},{"id":"s2","text":"approaching a stop intersection indicated by a stop sign","role":"trigger"},{"id":"s3","text":"shall stop before entering the crosswalk on the near side of the intersection or, if there is no crosswalk, shall stop at a clearly marked stop line, or if none, then at the point nearest the intersecting highway","role":"obligation"},{"id":"s4","text":"where the driver has a view of approaching traffic on the intersecting highway","role":"standard"},{"id":"s5","text":"before entering the intersection.","role":"condition"}],"elements":[{"span":"s1","atoms":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"],"derived":[],"justification":"“vehicle” is the term DEF-NRS-484A-320 defines and the run admits as the aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, so the span claims ru.aggregate with that id: the atom is “membership of a legal aggregate: the atom's literal argument is an aggregate id”, true where the road user carries an included class, unknown where an included or unresolved class it might carry is unobserved. Its exclusion “not a stand-in for a named road-user class” does not apply, because the admitted aggregate is claimed as the aggregate and never replaced by a class atom; its exclusion of “a relational role such as who drives or controls a vehicle” is respected by reading “driver” through the vehicle's controlled motion (narrowing on this span) rather than as a member of the aggregate."},{"span":"s2","atoms":["st.intersection","st.travel_region","rel.occupies","st.lane_enters","dev.stop_sign","dev.governs"],"derived":[],"justification":"The approach is read as the ontology's section on an act due at a place before an event states it: “a road user's approach to an intersection is a carrier it occupies (rel.occupies) whose entrance end is that intersection”. st.intersection is “the region where two roadways meet, bounded by the prolongation of their edges”, the region the words call the intersection; st.travel_region is the kind the carrier quantifier ranges over, “the union of the kinds a device can govern … a lane and the kinds that refine it, a bicycle lane or path, a roadway and the kinds that refine it, a shoulder, or an intersection”, which is exactly the set of carriers st.lane_enters admits, so each region argument of the claimed relations has a claimed kind; st.lane_enters is “the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end”, and its clause “it is entry topology: it is decided where the source records it … never inferred from distance, overlap or a road user's velocity” is why approaching is not read from heading or closing speed. dev.stop_sign is the “regulatory sign requiring a full halt”, the sign the words name, and dev.governs, “the travel regions whose traffic the device controls … or an intersection”, ties it to the carrier the vehicle approaches through, as the ontology directs (“the mark that governs that approach is one the source records as marking that carrier”); dev.governs's exclusion “not a stand-in for a position” does not apply, because the place of the halt is read from the crosswalk, the stop line or the view point in s3 and never from where the sign stands. rel.occupies is “a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region”, the anchor that makes the carrier the subject's own."},{"span":"s3","atoms":["st.crosswalk","st.stop_line","st.travel_region","st.entrance_of","st.lane_direction","st.region_geometry","rel.occupies","st.intersection","st.highway","st.on_way","prim.region_offset_along"],"derived":["drv.motion.standstill"],"justification":"“shall stop” is the act: drv.motion.standstill carries the posted definition DEF-NRS-484A-255, “complete cessation from movement”, as a motion state at an observation, with the speed tolerance the sampling leaves to the observer. The first place is the crosswalk “on the near side of the intersection”: st.crosswalk is the “marked crossing, or the unmarked prolongation of sidewalks at an intersection”, and which crossing is the near one is st.entrance_of, “the carrier whose entrance into an intersection a stop line or a crosswalk marks — exactly that carrier's entrance, the line or crossing a vehicle approaching through that carrier halts at or before”, read on the same carrier st.lane_enters relates to the intersection; st.entrance_of's exclusion “not a stand-in for distance to the line” is why nearness never selects the crossing. The second place is st.stop_line, “the transverse line marking where vehicles halt for a device”, taken where the crosswalk's observed list of entrances excludes the carrier, as st.entrance_of's completeness clause permits. The third is the point nearest the intersecting highway, read on the carrier (st.travel_region) against the way the junction lies on: st.highway is “the entire width between the boundary lines of every way”, st.on_way “the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on — … an intersection lies on every way that meets there”, so the intersecting highway is a way the intersection lies on other than the one the carrier lies on. That the halt is at the place and on the near side of it is st.region_geometry, “the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it”, within p.stop_point_tolerance, with the side taken from prim.region_offset_along, “the signed distance … measured along a carrier's designated direction (st.lane_direction)”, whose sign gives the side as the ontology requires (“the side of the mark is read along that carrier's designated direction … never along the road user's heading”); the primitive's own inputs are not claimed again beyond st.lane_direction and st.region_geometry, which the rule also reads on their own for the direction and for the distance, since prim.region_offset_along “is a geometric quantity only … a distance to the region is read from st.region_geometry, never from this value”. rel.occupies excludes a halt whose footprint already overlaps the crossing or the junction, which the words place the halt before, and st.intersection is the region that entry concerns."},{"span":"s5","atoms":["st.intersection","rel.occupies"],"derived":[],"justification":"“before entering the intersection” is the event the duty is owed before: the observation at which the vehicle's footprint first overlaps the intersection region. rel.occupies is “a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region (… intersection …)” and st.intersection the region itself; st.intersection's exclusion “not a stand-in for a crosswalk or a stop line — a stop before the crossing is earlier than a stop before the intersection” is precisely the distinction kept here, the crossing being the place of the act in s3 and the junction the event in this span."}],"operationalizations":[{"span":"s4","standard":"where the driver has a view of approaching traffic on the intersecting highway","concepts":["st.sight_along_way","st.highway","st.on_way","st.intersection","rel.visible","ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic","st.travel_region","rel.occupies"],"params":["p.intersecting_way_view_distance"],"convention":"Intersection sight-distance convention (AASHTO Green Book intersection sight distance, the departure-sight-triangle cases): a driver halted at the stopping point must be able to see along the major way at least the distance an approaching vehicle travels in the time needed to judge a gap and clear the junction. The point is adequate where st.sight_along_way, “the distance along a way, in each direction from the point of that way nearest a road user, within which another vehicle on that way could be seen from the road user's eye at the observation … the smaller of the two directions”, taken for the intersecting highway the junction lies on (st.highway with st.on_way and st.intersection), is at least p.intersecting_way_view_distance, and where a road user that is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic is on that way approaching the junction, that road user is visible from the vehicle (rel.visible, “b is visible from a: an unobstructed line of sight”). The aggregate fixes whose approach counts as the traffic to be seen — “pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances … using any highway for purposes of travel” — and the sight atom carries the view itself, since rel.visible “is not a stand-in for … the sight distance of a place” and st.sight_along_way is “not a stand-in for … whether an actual road user is seen”: the two together read the span's words where a road user is present and where none is. p.intersecting_way_view_distance is the only magnitude, and it is the reading's, not the words'.","surrogate":false}],"assumptions":[],"intentions":[],"compositions":[],"residues":[],"binders":[{"name":"v","class_elements":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"]}],"applicability":"The bound road user is a vehicle of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle that occupies a travel region whose entrance end is an intersection (st.lane_enters on that carrier) and that a stop sign governs (dev.stop_sign with dev.governs on that same carrier), and that enters that intersection: the stop intersection indicated by a stop sign which it approaches. Where the sign's governance of the carrier is unobserved, whether the rule applies is unknown; where the source's complete record shows the sign governs no carrier the vehicle occupies, the rule does not apply.","obligation":"At each observation at which the vehicle's footprint first overlaps the intersection it approaches (the entry event: the rise of rel.occupies of the vehicle on the intersection X that the carrier it occupies runs into, st.lane_enters, read from this observation and the one before it), the vehicle must have been at a standstill (drv.motion.standstill with p.standstill_speed_tolerance) at some observation of the approach that leads to that entry, with its body at the place the words name. The place is read from the words in their order: first the crosswalk that marks the entrance of the carrier the vehicle approaches through (st.entrance_of on the same carrier st.lane_enters relates to X); where that crosswalk's entrances are observed, so that its list is complete, and exclude the carrier, the clearly marked stop line that marks it; where neither marks it, the point on the carrier nearest the intersecting highway at which the view of s4 is met. Where a mark's association with the carrier is not observed, whether that mark governs is unknown and the duty is unknown on that ground. A halt counts at the place where the distance from the vehicle's body to the mark (st.region_geometry) is within p.stop_point_tolerance and the mark lies ahead along the carrier's designated direction (the sign of prim.region_offset_along with st.lane_direction); the words placing the halt before the vehicle enters the crossing and the junction, a halt at which its footprint already overlaps that region (rel.occupies) is not at the place, and the tolerance applies outside that region only. The search for the halt runs back from the entry event and ends only at the start of that approach — the last observation before the event at which the vehicle, on a carrier the mark marks, is off the mark, short of it and farther from it than p.stop_point_tolerance — or at the previous entry of the same vehicle into the same intersection; nothing else ends it: not another junction or mark, not the start of the recording, not a first observation, not a distance travelled. Only an observed exit from the stopping zone upstream begins a new approach, so a vehicle that leaves the zone upstream and returns owes the halt again, while crossing the mark, moving on toward the junction, a change of carrier, a lateral move or a reverse within the zone begin none and lose no halt already made. Where the search finds the halt the duty is met; where it reaches either end without the halt the duty is violated; where it reaches neither end without finding it — the recording begins inside the stopping zone, the observation before the event does not show the vehicle's place relative to the mark through its carrier, or the speed that decides the standstill is unobserved — the duty is unknown. Each entry owes its own halt: a halt made before the previous entry of the same vehicle into the same intersection discharged that entry, not this one.","params":["p.standstill_speed_tolerance","p.stop_point_tolerance","p.intersecting_way_view_distance"],"narrowings":[{"span":"s1","why":"“Every driver of a vehicle” is read as the vehicle whose motion is controlled. Who or what controls a road user is not observable, and the ontology reads “drives”, “operates” and “the driver” through the vehicle's controlled motion, a vehicle moving on the road being taken to be driven, with the duty binding that vehicle's conduct whoever or whatever is at the controls.","kind":"observable_reading","category":"agency"},{"span":"s2","why":"“indicated by a stop sign” is read as the presence of a stop sign governing the approach. That a sign is official or posted by an authority is a legal status the ontology reads through the feature itself: the sign's presence on the road is the evidence of the designation the section's title speaks of.","kind":"observable_reading","category":"status"},{"span":"s3","why":"“a clearly marked stop line” is read as the stop line the scene represents. The ontology states this reading for exactly these words: the line's presence is the evidence, and the paint's clarity or wear is not modelled. The reading relaxes nothing about which place governs, the act or its timing.","kind":"observable_reading","category":"status"},{"span":"s3","why":"“the point nearest the intersecting highway where the driver has a view” is read as a point on the carrier the vehicle approaches through, rather than any point of the scene: the words single out the vehicle's own approach, and the place is read on the region the node binds. Among the points of that carrier at which the view of s4 is met, the duty is read as met by a halt at or before the nearest such point to the intersecting highway, within p.stop_point_tolerance of it, so a halt farther back on the same carrier that still meets the view is not a violation; this is the reading of “the point nearest … where the driver has a view”, which names a nearest point among those with a view and not a single surveyed spot.","kind":"reading"},{"span":"s4","why":"“the driver has a view of approaching traffic” is read as what could be seen along the intersecting way from where the vehicle stands, and as the visibility of a road user of the traffic aggregate that is there. What a driver perceived is not observable; the ontology directs that where the words offer observable evidence the rule reads it, “what was in an actual road user's line of sight is rel.visible; what could be seen from or at a place is st.sight_distance”, and st.sight_along_way is that quantity measured along the way for a road user at the observation.","kind":"observable_reading","category":"perception"}],"scenarios":[{"name":"forbid","expected":"violated","narrative":"A car runs along a marked lane that the source records as entering a four-way junction, and a stop sign governs that lane. A marked crosswalk is recorded as marking that lane's entrance. From the last observation at which the car is off the crossing, short of it and more than the stop-point tolerance from it, through to the observation at which its footprint first overlaps the junction, its speed never falls to the standstill tolerance: it rolls over the crossing at about 4 m/s and enters the junction.","masked":[]},{"name":"permit","expected":"compliant","narrative":"The same approach and the same crossing. Two seconds before the crossing the car's speed falls to zero and stays there for several observations, its body short of the crossing along the lane's designated direction and within the stop-point tolerance of it, its footprint overlapping neither the crossing nor the junction; it then moves off and enters the junction.","masked":[]},{"name":"idle","expected":"not_applicable","narrative":"A pedal cycle propelled by human power — a device the vehicle definition leaves out, so the aggregate is false for it — rides along the same stop-sign-governed lane and into the junction without halting anywhere. Not a stand-in for: the gear selected — a body in a forward gear rolls backwards on a grade and one in reverse stands still — a reversing lamp or any other signal, a halt, a turn, or the place the motion happens at.","definition":null,"args":[{"name":"u","sort":"track"}],"params":[{"name":"reverse_speed_tolerance","unit":"m/s","meaning":"the magnitude of the rearward velocity component below which the motion is not distinguished from a standing body's measurement noise; it names the source's resolution"}],"elements":[{"span":"the component of its velocity along the direction its body points","atoms":["kin.velocity","kin.heading"],"concepts":[],"justification":"kin.velocity is the “velocity vector” in m/s in the world frame and kin.heading the “direction the body points”, which “a formula reads … normalised”, so the product of the two along the heading is the signed speed in the direction the body points. The ontology directs this reading expressly: kin.gear is “not a stand-in for the direction of motion — a vehicle in a forward gear rolls backwards on a grade; backing is read from kinematics”. kin.speed is not read, being unsigned."}],"residues":[],"literals":[],"scenarios":[{"name":"holds","expected":"compliant","narrative":"A car reverses out of a parking bay at about 1.5 m/s: its velocity points opposite to its heading, so the component along the heading is about minus 1.5 m/s.","masked":[]},{"name":"fails","expected":"violated","narrative":"The same car drives forward out of the bay at 1.5 m/s: the component along its heading is about plus 1.5 m/s.","masked":[]},{"name":"blind","expected":"unknown","narrative":"The same manoeuvre with the source declaring road-user velocity absent: the direction of the motion relative to the body cannot be read.","masked":["kin.velocity"]}],"used_by":["NRS_484B_113_2"],"supersedes":null}
{"concept_id":"drv.motion.turning","kind":"formula","contract":"The road user's heading is changing at the observation: the magnitude of its heading change over the window behind the observation is at least the heading change tolerance, a size the caller sets at the resolution of the source. It is a state the road user is in at each observation of a bending path, in either hand, and it states no direction, no angle reached, no beginning and no place. Not a stand-in for: a completed turn or a manoeuvre recognized from an observed onset — which counts the heading change from that onset and not over a window — a steering input, the curvature of the road, a lane change, or a signal or an intention.","definition":null,"args":[{"name":"u","sort":"track"}],"params":[{"name":"window","unit":"s","meaning":"the length of the window behind the observation over which the heading change is accumulated"},{"name":"heading_change_tolerance","unit":"deg","meaning":"the magnitude of heading change over that window below which the reading is not distinguished from straight running; it names the source's resolution and no size of turn"}],"elements":[{"span":"the magnitude of its heading change over the window behind the observation","atoms":["prim.heading_change"],"concepts":[],"justification":"prim.heading_change is “the signed heading change (degrees, left positive) of a road user over the window behind the observation, integrated from kin.yaw_rate; unknown where the window is truncated, sampled too sparsely, or a yaw rate is missing”, whose magnitude is exactly the quantity this contract bounds, and whose window is its own parameter, which this concept exposes. Its inputs are the primitive's own and are not claimed again."}],"residues":[],"literals":[],"scenarios":[{"name":"holds","expected":"compliant","narrative":"A van swings round the corner of a junction: over the window behind the observation its integrated heading change is about forty degrees, well above the tolerance.","masked":[]},{"name":"fails","expected":"violated","narrative":"The same van reverses straight back along a roadway: its integrated heading change over the window is under a degree, below the tolerance.","masked":[]},{"name":"blind","expected":"unknown","narrative":"The corner manoeuvre at the start of the recording, where the window behind the observation is truncated, so the primitive's integration is unknown.","masked":["kin.yaw_rate"]}],"used_by":["NRS_484B_113_2"],"supersedes":null}
{"concept_id":"drv.interaction.following","kind":"formula","contract":"Road user a is following road user b at the observation: b is ahead of a in the same lane along that lane's direction of travel, and the two bodies' headings are aligned within the same-direction tolerance, a cosine the caller sets. no other atom carries an in-lane order, rel.bearing giving only a direction in the subject's frame."},{"span":"the two bodies' headings are aligned within the same-direction tolerance","atoms":["rel.same_direction"],"concepts":[],"justification":"rel.same_direction is “headings aligned: the cosine of the angle between the headings is above its tolerance, which is the cosine of the largest angle allowed, a ratio between -1 and 1”; the tolerance is the atom's own parameter, which this concept exposes as its formal parameter."}],"residues":[],"literals":[],"scenarios":[{"name":"holds","expected":"compliant","narrative":"A car runs in the same lane as a van, 30 m behind it, both headings within a few degrees of each other along the lane.","masked":[]},{"name":"fails","expected":"violated","narrative":"The car runs abreast of the van in the neighbouring lane: neither is ahead of the other in the same lane.","masked":[]},{"name":"blind","expected":"unknown","narrative":"The same pair with the source declaring the in-lane order of road users absent: whether the van is ahead of the car in its lane cannot be read.","masked":["rel.ahead_behind_in_lane"]}],"used_by":["NRS_484B_127_1","NRS_484B_127_2"],"supersedes":null}
{"concept_id":"drv.interaction.overtaking","kind":"formula","contract":"Road user a is passing road user b at the observation: the two headings are aligned within the same-direction tolerance, a's speed exceeds b's by at least the speed excess the caller sets, and either the two bodies' projections on a's heading overlap — a is drawing level with b — or b is still ahead of a in the same lane. It is the state of a passing manoeuvre at the observation and states no lane used, no clearance between the bodies, no completion of the pass and no right to make it. Not a stand-in for: a completed pass, the lane or side the pass is made on, a signal or an intention, or the clearance between the bodies, which the gap atom carries.","definition":null,"args":[{"name":"a","sort":"track"},{"name":"b","sort":"track"}],"params":[{"name":"same_direction_tolerance","unit":"1","meaning":"the cosine of the largest angle between the two headings still read as the same direction, a ratio between minus one and one"},{"name":"min_speed_excess","unit":"m/s","meaning":"the amount by which a's speed must exceed b's for the two to be read as passing rather than keeping station; it names the resolution of a speed difference"}],"elements":[{"span":"the two headings are aligned within the same-direction tolerance","atoms":["rel.same_direction"],"concepts":[],"justification":"rel.same_direction is “headings aligned: the cosine of the angle between the headings is above its tolerance”, the relation this clause states, with the tolerance the atom's own parameter."},{"span":"a's speed exceeds b's by at least the speed excess","atoms":["kin.speed"],"concepts":[],"justification":"kin.speed is the “magnitude of velocity” in m/s of each road user, so the difference of the two readings is the excess this clause bounds; kin.accel_longitudinal is excluded by its own contract as “not a stand-in for speed”."},{"span":"the two bodies' projections on a's heading overlap","atoms":["rel.longitudinal_overlap"],"concepts":[],"justification":"rel.longitudinal_overlap is “the bodies overlap along the subject's heading (side by side): the length the two footprints' projections on that axis share, negative for the gap between the projections; a projection, so neither a contact nor a distance between the bodies”, which is the drawing level this clause states."},{"span":"b is still ahead of a in the same lane","atoms":["rel.ahead_behind_in_lane"],"concepts":[],"justification":"rel.ahead_behind_in_lane is “a is ahead of / behind b in the same lane, along the lane direction”, which carries the earlier part of a pass, before the bodies draw level."}],"residues":[],"literals":[],"scenarios":[{"name":"holds","expected":"compliant","narrative":"A lorry at 24 m/s draws level with a lorry at 20 m/s on a two-lane highway, their headings aligned and their bodies' projections on the overtaking lorry's heading sharing several metres.","masked":[]},{"name":"fails","expected":"violated","narrative":"The two lorries run in file at the same speed, 40 m apart: there is no speed excess, so neither is passing the other.","masked":[]},{"name":"blind","expected":"unknown","narrative":"The same pair drawing level with the source declaring the speed of road users absent: whether one is gaining on the other cannot be read.","masked":["kin.speed"]}],"used_by":["NRS_484B_127_2"],"supersedes":null,"differs_from":{"concept":"drv.interaction.following","why":"The two take the same sorts — two road users — but read different atoms and decide differently for the same motion: following reads only the in-lane order and the heading agreement, and is true of a pair that keeps station indefinitely, while passing adds the speed excess and the longitudinal overlap of the bodies and is false of such a pair."}}
{"concept_id":"drv.interaction.vehicle_file","kind":"formula","contract":"Road user u is one of a file of road users travelling one behind another at the observation: counting u itself, at least the minimum member count of road users have their heading aligned with u's within the same-direction tolerance, lie ahead of or behind u in the same lane, and are within the file reach of u, a distance the caller sets measured between the nearest points of the bodies. It is a relation of place, direction and spacing at the observation. It says nothing of why the road users travel together, of a common destination or origin, of an organizer, or of their speed: a caller that means a moving file states the motion itself. Not a stand-in for: a chain each of whose consecutive spaces is bounded — the reach is measured from u to each member, so a long file is read through the membership of each road user in turn — the class of the members, which the caller states, or a towed combination, which is one road user drawn by another.","definition":null,"args":[{"name":"u","sort":"track"}],"params":[{"name":"min_member_count","unit":"1","meaning":"the number of road users, u included, at which the group is read as a file rather than as road users happening to follow one another"},{"name":"file_reach","unit":"m","meaning":"the distance between the nearest points of two bodies within which another road user is read as travelling with u in the same file"},{"name":"same_direction_tolerance","unit":"1","meaning":"the cosine of the largest angle between two headings still read as the same direction, a ratio between minus one and one"}],"elements":[{"span":"have their heading aligned with u's within the same-direction tolerance","atoms":["rel.same_direction"],"concepts":[],"justification":"rel.same_direction is “headings aligned: the cosine of the angle between the headings is above its tolerance”, the relation this clause states, the tolerance being the atom's own parameter."},{"span":"lie ahead of or behind u in the same lane","atoms":["rel.ahead_behind_in_lane"],"concepts":[],"justification":"rel.ahead_behind_in_lane is “a is ahead of / behind b in the same lane, along the lane direction”, which is the one-behind-another arrangement this clause states; rel.bearing is not read, giving only a direction and not an in-lane order."},{"span":"are within the file reach of u, a distance … measured between the nearest points of the bodies","atoms":["rel.surface_gap"],"concepts":[],"justification":"rel.surface_gap is the “distance between the nearest points of two bodies, each body's footprint read with its own heading and extent”, which is the spacing this clause bounds; rel.centre_distance is excluded by its own contract as “not a stand-in for a clearance between bodies”."}],"residues":[],"literals":[],"scenarios":[{"name":"holds","expected":"compliant","narrative":"Five cars run in file in one lane of a rural highway, each within 20 m of the next and all headings aligned: each of them, counting itself, has at least three members of the group within the reach, ahead of or behind it in the lane.","masked":[]},{"name":"fails","expected":"violated","narrative":"One car runs alone in that lane with the nearest other road user 400 m ahead: the minimum member count is not reached within the reach.","masked":[]},{"name":"blind","expected":"unknown","narrative":"The five cars with the source declaring the gap between bodies absent: how far apart the members are, and so how many lie within the reach, cannot be read.","masked":["rel.surface_gap"]}],"used_by":["NRS_484B_127_3"],"supersedes":null}
{"concept_id":"drv.position.direction_component","kind":"quantity","contract":"The component, in metres per second, of a road user's velocity along the designated direction of travel of a structure region: positive where the road user moves with that direction, negative where it moves against it, and near zero where it stands or moves across it. The region's direction is read normalised, as its atom states, so the value is a speed along that direction. The quantity is geometric only: it does not state that the road user is on the region, that the region is the one a law names, or how far the road user is from it, and a caller states those with its own relations. Unknown where the road user's velocity is absent and where the region carries no designated direction — a centre turn lane carries none, and a place no carrier covers has none. Not a stand-in for: the direction the body points, which a road user may hold while moving another way, the road user's speed, which is unsigned, or an angle between the two directions.","definition":null,"args":[{"name":"u","sort":"track"},{"name":"r","sort":"region"}],"params":[],"elements":[{"span":"a road user's velocity","atoms":["kin.velocity"],"concepts":[],"justification":"kin.velocity is the “velocity vector” of a road user, in m/s in the world frame, whose components are what this quantity projects; kin.speed is not read, being the unsigned magnitude, and kin.heading is excluded because the contract reads the direction of the motion and not the direction the body points."},{"span":"the designated direction of travel of a structure region","atoms":["st.lane_direction"],"concepts":[],"justification":"st.lane_direction is the “direction of travel designated for a structure a vehicle travels in — a lane, reserved lane, turn lane, bicycle lane or path, or a roadway, one-way roadway or shoulder”, which “a formula reads … normalised”, exactly as this contract reads it, and whose contract also states that “a centre turn lane carries none” and “a place no carrier covers has none (unknown)”, which the contract's unknown clause carries."}],"residues":[],"literals":[],"scenarios":[{"name":"holds","expected":"compliant","narrative":"A car travels at 8 m/s along a one-way roadway whose designated direction runs the same way: the quantity reads about plus 8 m/s, within bounds the caller sets for travel with the designation.","masked":[]},{"name":"fails","expected":"violated","narrative":"The same car travels at 8 m/s the other way along that roadway: the quantity reads about minus 8 m/s, outside those bounds.","masked":[]},{"name":"blind","expected":"unknown","narrative":"The same roadway with the source declaring the designated direction of travel of structures absent: the quantity has no direction to project onto and is unknown.","masked":["st.lane_direction"]}],"used_by":["NRS_484B_220_1","NRS_484B_227_1_o1"],"supersedes":null}
{"concept_id":"drv.lane.lane_change","kind":"formula","contract":"The road user crosses out of a structure region at the observation: its footprint overlapped the region at the observation before, and at the observation it either no longer overlaps that region or overlaps a lane neighbouring it in the same direction of travel which it did not overlap at the observation before. Not a stand-in for: a turn, since no heading change is read, a signal or a declared intention, a movement that stays within the region however far across it, the completion of a movement into the neighbouring region, or the direction or side the crossing is made towards, which a caller reads from the regions themselves.","definition":null,"args":[{"name":"u","sort":"track"},{"name":"r","sort":"region"}],"params":[],"elements":[{"span":"its footprint overlapped the region at the observation before","atoms":["rel.occupies"],"concepts":[],"justification":"rel.occupies is “a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region (roadway, shoulder, sidewalk, intersection, crosswalk …)”, which is the occupancy this clause reads, taken at the previous observation by the formula language's own past reading; st.region_geometry is excluded by its own contract, which states that “a footprint inside a boundary is rel.occupies”."},{"span":"overlaps a lane neighbouring it in the same direction of travel","atoms":["rel.occupies","st.lane_adjacency","st.lane"],"concepts":[],"justification":"st.lane_adjacency is the “left / right neighbouring lane of the same direction”, which is the neighbour this clause names, and its exclusion “not a stand-in for the marking between two lanes” does not apply, since the neighbour and not the mark is read; the neighbour is a region of kind st.lane, “a longitudinal strip of roadway for one line of vehicles”, which the body's quantifier ranges over, and rel.occupies is the overlap of the footprint with it."}],"residues":[],"literals":[],"scenarios":[{"name":"holds","expected":"compliant","narrative":"A car running in the middle lane of a three-lane carriageway reaches the left-hand lane: at the observation before, its footprint overlapped the middle lane alone; at the observation it overlaps the left-hand lane as well.","masked":[]},{"name":"fails","expected":"violated","narrative":"The same car drifts to the left within the middle lane and back again: its footprint overlaps the middle lane and no neighbouring lane at every observation.","masked":[]},{"name":"blind","expected":"unknown","narrative":"The same movement with the source declaring the occupancy of regions by road users absent: whether the footprint overlapped the lane before and the neighbour now cannot be read.","masked":["rel.occupies"]}],"used_by":["NRS_484B_223_1b"],"supersedes":null}
{"concept_id":"drv.motion.left_turn","kind":"formula","contract":"The road user has turned to the left: counting from the onset of the turning — the observation at which its rate of change of heading to the left first rose above the onset yaw rate, a rate the caller sets — the heading change accumulated since that onset reaches at least the turn angle, a size the caller sets, to the left. The concept becomes true at the observation at which that angle is first reached and stays true at the later observations at which the accumulated change still holds it, until a later onset starts the count again; the integration is bounded by the heading step, the largest interval between consecutive observations it may integrate across. It states the turning of the body only: no place, no lane, no way and no destination. Not a stand-in for: a signal or a declared intention, a steering input, the curvature of the road — a body yaws on a straight road whenever it manoeuvres — a lane change, or a reversal of the direction of travel, which is a larger angle and has its own concept.","definition":null,"args":[{"name":"u","sort":"track"}],"params":[{"name":"heading_step","unit":"ms","meaning":"the largest interval between two consecutive observations the heading integration may cross, the sampling standard of the acquisition profile"},{"name":"onset_yaw_rate","unit":"deg/s","meaning":"the rate of change of heading above which the body is read as beginning to turn rather than running straight, which fixes the observed onset the heading change is counted from"},{"name":"turn_angle","unit":"deg","meaning":"the accumulated heading change at which a turn to the left is recognized"}],"act":{"boundary":"event","onset":"the observation at which its rate of change of heading to the left first rose above the onset yaw rate","recognition":"the observation at which the heading change accumulated since that onset reaches at least the turn angle","extent":"the later observations at which the accumulated change still holds the turn angle, until a later onset starts the count again","history":"the onset must be observed, with the rate of change of heading known at every observation from the one before it onwards and no interval between consecutive observations longer than the heading step; where no such onset is observed within the recording, or a yaw rate since it is missing, the concept is unknown and never false"},"elements":[{"span":"its rate of change of heading to the left first rose above the onset yaw rate","atoms":["kin.yaw_rate"],"concepts":[],"justification":"kin.yaw_rate is the “rate of change of heading, positive when the heading turns to the left (counter-clockwise)”, in deg/s, which is the quantity whose rise marks the onset; its exclusion “not a stand-in for road curvature — a vehicle yaws on a straight road whenever it manoeuvres” does not apply, because the body's yaw and not the road's bend is what the contract reads."},{"span":"the heading change accumulated since that onset","atoms":["kin.yaw_rate"],"concepts":[],"justification":"The accumulated heading change since an observed onset is integrated from the same atom by the formula language's own construct, which the ontology describes as “the signed heading change of a road user since a formula last became true, integrated from kin.yaw_rate with a step bound”; prim.heading_change is expressly “not a stand-in for it”, being taken over a fixed window behind each observation rather than from an onset, which is why this concept reads the atom and not that primitive."}],"residues":[],"literals":[],"scenarios":[{"name":"holds","expected":"compliant","narrative":"A car running straight begins to swing left: its yaw rate rises above the onset rate, and a second and a half later the heading change accumulated since that observation passes the turn angle.","masked":[]},{"name":"fails","expected":"violated","narrative":"The same car changes lane to the left: its yaw rate rises above the onset rate briefly, but the accumulated heading change peaks at a few degrees and never reaches the turn angle.","masked":[]},{"name":"blind","expected":"unknown","narrative":"The car is already turning at the first observation of the recording, so no onset is observed with the yaw rate known at every observation since: the accumulated change cannot be counted.","masked":["kin.yaw_rate"]}],"used_by":["NRS_484B_227_1_o2"],"supersedes":null}
{"concept_id":"drv.motion.u_turn","kind":"formula","contract":"The road user's direction of travel upon a way has reversed: counting from the onset of the manoeuvre — the observation at which the magnitude of its rate of change of heading first rose above the onset yaw rate, a rate the caller sets — the magnitude of the heading change accumulated since that onset reaches at least the reversal angle, a size the caller sets below a half turn, while the road user's footprint overlaps a way. The definition this contract carries is the turning of a vehicle upon a highway “so as to proceed in the opposite direction”, “whether accomplished by one continuous movement or not”, so halts, rearward movements and steering the other way between the onset and the reversal do not end the manoeuvre, and the count runs on until the angle is reached or a later onset starts it again; the integration is bounded by the heading step, the largest interval between consecutive observations it may integrate across. The reversal angle is the contract's own magnitude, the bound within which a sampled heading change is read as the opposite direction. Not a stand-in for: a turn through a smaller angle, which has its own concept, a turn into another way, travel against a designated direction of travel, a reversing movement, or a signal or a declared intention.","definition":"DEF-NRS-484B-077","args":[{"name":"u","sort":"track"}],"params":[{"name":"heading_step","unit":"ms","meaning":"the largest interval between two consecutive observations the heading integration may cross, the sampling standard of the acquisition profile"},{"name":"onset_yaw_rate","unit":"deg/s","meaning":"the rate of change of heading above which the body is read as beginning to turn rather than running straight, which fixes the observed onset the heading change is counted from"},{"name":"reversal_angle","unit":"deg","meaning":"the accumulated heading change at which the definition's proceeding in the opposite direction is recognized; its exclusion of road curvature does not apply, the body's yaw being what is read."},{"span":"the magnitude of the heading change accumulated since that onset","atoms":["kin.yaw_rate"],"concepts":[],"justification":"The accumulated heading change since an observed onset is integrated from the same atom by the formula language's own construct, “the signed heading change of a road user since a formula last became true, integrated from kin.yaw_rate with a step bound”; the concept is written for any road user and adds no class of its own."}],"literals":[],"scenarios":[{"name":"holds","expected":"compliant","narrative":"A car on a city street swings left across the way, halts to let a vehicle pass, reverses a metre and completes the swing: from the onset of the turning the accumulated heading change reaches about a hundred and seventy degrees while its footprint overlaps the way.","masked":[]},{"name":"fails","expected":"violated","narrative":"The same car turns left into a side street: the accumulated heading change since the onset peaks at about ninety degrees and never reaches the reversal angle.","masked":[]},{"name":"blind","expected":"unknown","narrative":"The car is already mid-turn at the first observation of the recording, so no onset is observed with the yaw rate known at every observation since: whether the direction reversed cannot be read.","masked":["kin.yaw_rate"]}],"used_by":["NRS_484B_227_1_o2"],"supersedes":null,"differs_from":{"concept":"drv.motion.left_turn","why":"Both take one road user and read the same atom, but they recognize different manoeuvres and decide differently for the same motion: the left turn is recognized at a smaller angle to the left alone, while this concept reads the magnitude of the accumulated change, so it holds for a reversal to either hand and is false of an ordinary junction turn that the left-turn concept recognizes."}}

lines: {"node_id":"NRS_484A_450_2","law_refs":["NRS-484A-450-2"],"subject":{"binder":"v","class_elements":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"]},"segmentation":[{"id":"s1","text":"Every driver of a vehicle","role":"subject"},{"id":"s2","text":"approaching a stop intersection indicated by a stop sign","role":"trigger"},{"id":"s3","text":"shall stop before entering the crosswalk on the near side of the intersection or, if there is no crosswalk, shall stop at a clearly marked stop line, or if none, then at the point nearest the intersecting highway","role":"obligation"},{"id":"s4","text":"where the driver has a view of approaching traffic on the intersecting highway","role":"standard"},{"id":"s5","text":"before entering the intersection.","role":"condition"}],"elements":[{"span":"s1","atoms":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"],"derived":[],"justification":"“vehicle” is the term DEF-NRS-484A-320 defines and the run admits as the aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, so the span claims ru.aggregate with that id: the atom is “membership of a legal aggregate: the atom's literal argument is an aggregate id”, true where the road user carries an included class, unknown where an included or unresolved class it might carry is unobserved. Its exclusion “not a stand-in for a named road-user class” does not apply, because the admitted aggregate is claimed as the aggregate and never replaced by a class atom; its exclusion of “a relational role such as who drives or controls a vehicle” is respected by reading “driver” through the vehicle's controlled motion (narrowing on this span) rather than as a member of the aggregate."},{"span":"s2","atoms":["st.intersection","st.travel_region","rel.occupies","st.lane_enters","dev.stop_sign","dev.governs"],"derived":[],"justification":"The approach is read as the ontology's section on an act due at a place before an event states it: “a road user's approach to an intersection is a carrier it occupies (rel.occupies) whose entrance end is that intersection”. st.intersection is “the region where two roadways meet, bounded by the prolongation of their edges”, the region the words call the intersection; {"node_id":"NRS_484B_127_2","law_refs":["NRS-484B-127-2"],"subject":{"binder":"v","class_elements":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-305::truck","ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-050::combination_of_vehicles","kin.extent"]},"segmentation":[{"id":"s1","text":"The driver of any truck or combination of vehicles 80 inches or more in overall width,","role":"subject"},{"id":"s2","text":"which is following a truck, or combination of vehicles 80 inches or more in overall width,","role":"trigger"},{"id":"s3","text":"shall, whenever conditions permit,","role":"standard"},{"id":"s4","text":"leave a space of 500 feet","role":"obligation"},{"id":"s5","text":"so that an overtaking vehicle may enter and occupy such space without danger,","role":"condition"},{"id":"s6","text":"but this shall not prevent a truck or combination of vehicles from overtaking and passing any vehicle or combination of vehicles.","role":"exception"},{"id":"s7","text":"This subsection does not apply to any vehicle or combination of vehicles while moving on a highway on which there are two or more lanes available for traffic moving in the same direction.","role":"exception"}],"elements":[{"span":"s1","atoms":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-305::truck","ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-050::combination_of_vehicles","kin.extent"],"derived":[],"justification":"“truck” and “combination of vehicles” are terms DEF-NRS-484A-305 and DEF-NRS-484A-050 define and the run admits as the aggregates DEF-NRS-484A-305::truck and DEF-NRS-484A-050::combination_of_vehicles, so the span claims ru.aggregate with each id and never the class atoms ru.truck or ru.trailer_or_combination, which the aggregate's exclusion forbids as a substitute. {"concept_id":"drv.motion.left_turn","kind":"formula","contract":"The road user has turned to the left: counting from the onset of the turning — the observation at which its rate of change of heading to the left first rose above the onset yaw rate, a rate the caller sets — the heading change accumulated since that onset reaches at least the turn angle, a size the caller sets, to the left. {"node_id":"NRS_484B_223_1b","law_refs":["NRS-484B-223-1b"],"subject":{"binder":"v","class_elements":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"]},"segmentation":[{"id":"s1","text":"If a highway has two or more clearly marked lanes for traffic traveling in one direction,","role":"trigger"},{"id":"s2","text":"vehicles must:","role":"subject"},{"id":"s3","text":"Not be moved from that lane","role":"obligation"},{"id":"s4","text":"until the driver has given the appropriate turn signal","role":"condition"},{"id":"s5","text":"and ascertained that such movement can be made with traffic”, DEF-NRS-484A-095's words, anchored to the subject by rel.occupies and tied to the lanes by st.on_way, “the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on — a lane, roadway, shoulder …”. “two or more … lanes … traveling in one direction” is st.lane, “a longitudinal strip of roadway for one line of vehicles”, with st.lane_adjacency, which carries “lane ordinal within the carriageway and the count of lanes in that direction”, the count the words require, and st.lane_direction, “direction of travel designated for a structure a vehicle travels in”, which fixes that the lanes counted are those of one direction — the direction of the lane the subject occupies. st.lane's exclusion “not a stand-in for a half of the roadway or a lateral position within a lane” is respected: the rule reads the mapped lanes and their count, not an offset from the edge. “clearly marked” is read through st.lane_marking, “per side of a lane: type ∈ {none, broken, solid, double_solid, solid_broken, dotted, curb}, colour …”: a lane marked on the side the movement crosses carries a marking of a type other than none, and the clarity of the paint is not modelled (narrowing on this span). “traffic” claims its admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic, which fixes whose travel the lanes are for. The literal two is the law's own figure."},{"span":"s2","atoms":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"],"derived":[],"justification":"“vehicles” is the term DEF-NRS-484A-320 defines and the run admits as DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, so the span claims ru.aggregate with that id and never the classes it covers."},{"span":"s3","atoms":["st.lane","rel.occupies"],"derived":["drv.lane.lane_change"],"justification":"“moved from that lane” is a manoeuvre and maps to a concept: drv.lane.lane_change states that the road user's footprint overlapped the region at the observation before and that at the observation it either no longer overlaps it or overlaps a lane adjacent to it that it did not overlap before, built on rel.occupies, “a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region”, and st.lane_adjacency, “left / right neighbouring lane of the same direction”. The concept takes the lane as a region formal, so the lane it reads is the one “that lane” singles out — the marked lane the trigger binds for the subject — and not any lane of the scene. st.lane is the kind that region argument admits and rel.occupies the anchor; the heading change is not read, since the words forbid the movement out of the lane and not a turn."},{"span":"s4","atoms":["sig.turn_indicator","sig.hand_signal","st.lane_adjacency","st.lane"],"derived":[],"justification":"“the appropriate turn signal” is the signal the vehicle emits: sig.turn_indicator is “the turn indicator state ∈ {off, left, right}: neither indicator lit, or the left or the right one”, and sig.hand_signal “a driver's or rider's arm signal; meaning ∈ {no_signal, left, right, stop_or_slow, re_enter}”, which is the other way the same indication is given and which the law's own scheme admits. sig.turn_indicator's exclusion “not a stand-in for the turn or lane change itself — the indicator is the signal that precedes a manoeuvre, judged separately from it” is exactly the separation these words make, the manoeuvre being s3's concept.
