The movement can be made with safety at the observation of the change where, for every road user of DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic other than the subject that occupies the lane the subject moves into (rel.occupies with st.lane) or lies alongside the subject: the longitudinal component of rel.surface_gap, “distance between the nearest points of two bodies … its longitudinal and lateral components”, is at least p.lane_change_min_clearance + p.lane_change_entry_headway_time × the greater of the two kin.speed readings, so the required clearance grows with the speed of the faster of the pair; and the two do not close to less than p.lane_change_min_clearance within the horizon, which prim.closest_approach_within, “under constant velocities, the centres of two road users approach each other at some time between the observation and the horizon”, and prim.closest_approach_distance, “the centre distance at that closest approach”, decide over p.lane_change_conflict_horizon. drv.lane.lane_change fixes the observation and the lane the test is made for. L is the lane the words single out as “that lane”: the obligation binds it again with the whole of that selection — a lane of the same highway, in a direction with at least two lanes, marked, and occupied by the subject at the observation before the movement — and the duty is written for every such lane the subject occupies, since the words require it of each.","obligation":"At each observation at which the subject moves out of such a lane L (drv.lane.lane_change for the subject and L), the appropriate turn signal must have been given for that movement and the movement must be one that can be made with safety on the bound of s5. rel.occupies anchors it to the subject and st.on_way, “the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on”, ties the travelled region to that way. “designated … for one-way traffic” is carried twice over, as the ontology's vocabulary carries it: st.one_way_roadway is the “roadway on which traffic is restricted to one direction”, a refinement of st.roadway, and st.lane_direction is the “direction of travel designated for a structure a vehicle travels in — a lane, reserved lane, turn lane, bicycle lane or path, or a roadway, one-way roadway or shoulder”, which is the designation the next span reads; st.travel_region is the kind the quantifier over the travelled region ranges over, the abstract union that admits the lane, roadway, one-way roadway and shoulder the direction may be carried on. “signposted” is dev.regulatory_sign with code one_way, “a point regulation by catalogue code … one_way”, tied to the region by dev.governs, “the travel regions whose traffic the device controls”, and its conditions are read by prim.conditions_hold, “the structured conditions of a device … hold at the observation”, since the sign's row directs that its conditions are read that way (unconditional when empty, unknown when absent); dev.regulatory_sign's exclusion “not a stand-in for a manoeuvre or a road feature” does not apply, because the designated direction itself is read from st.lane_direction and the sign carries only the posting. “traffic” claims its admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic — “pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances either singly or together using any highway for purposes of travel” — which fixes whose travel the one-way designation governs."},{"span":"s2","atoms":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"],"derived":[],"justification":"“vehicle” is the term DEF-NRS-484A-320 defines and the run admits as DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, so the span claims ru.aggregate with that id: “membership of a legal aggregate … true when the user carries an included class, unknown when … an included or unresolved class it might carry is unobserved”. The aggregate is claimed whole and never expanded into classes."},{"span":"s3","atoms":["rel.occupies","st.travel_region","st.lane_direction"],"derived":["drv.position.direction_component"],"justification":"“driven only in the direction designated” compares the vehicle's direction of travel with the designated direction of the region it occupies: drv.position.direction_component is the component of its velocity along that region's designated direction, positive with the designation and negative against it, built on kin.velocity, “velocity vector”, and st.lane_direction, read normalised as that atom's contract directs. rel.occupies is the anchor that makes the region the vehicle's own, and st.travel_region the kind its quantifier ranges over, the abstract union that admits the lane, one-way roadway, roadway and shoulder a designated direction may be carried on. “driven” is read through controlled motion (narrowing on this span); kin.heading is not read, because a vehicle may point one way while moving another and the words govern the direction it is driven in."}],"operationalizations":[],"assumptions":[],"intentions":[],"compositions":[],"residues":[],"binders":[{"name":"v","class_elements":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"]}],"applicability":"The bound road user is a vehicle of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle whose footprint overlaps a travel region that lies on a highway and that carries a designated direction of travel, where a regulatory sign of code one_way governs that region and its posted conditions hold at the observation. Where the sign's governance or its conditions are unobserved, whether the rule applies is unknown; where no such sign governs the region, the rule does not apply.","obligation":"At each observation at which the applicability holds, the component of the vehicle's velocity along the designated direction of the region it occupies (drv.position.direction_component) must not be at or below the negative of p.wrong_way_speed_tolerance: a component below that is travel against the designated direction and the duty is violated. A component above it — travel with the designation, a standstill, or a movement across the region within the tolerance — complies. Where the velocity or the region's designated direction is unobserved the duty is unknown. Where the vehicle occupies several such regions and the verdict differs between them, the duty is unknown; where it is the same through each, it is decided.","params":["p.wrong_way_speed_tolerance"],"narrowings":[{"span":"s1","why":"“designated and signposted” is read as the presence of a one-way regulatory sign governing the region and of a designated direction of travel on it. The component of its velocity along the designated direction is about minus 8 m/s.","masked":[]},{"name":"permit","expected":"compliant","narrative":"The same car on the same signposted one-way roadway travelling at 8 m/s with the designated direction: the component of its velocity along that direction is about plus 8 m/s.","masked":[]},{"name":"idle","expected":"not_applicable","narrative":"A car travels along a two-way roadway against the flow in the oncoming lane. No one-way regulatory sign governs the region it occupies, so the trigger of this subsection fails and the rule does not engage.","masked":[]},{"name":"blind","expected":"unknown","narrative":"The forbid scene with the source declaring the designated direction of travel of structures absent: the one-way sign and its governance of the roadway are recorded and the car's velocity is recorded, but the direction the words compare it with cannot be read, so the duty is unknown.","masked":["st.lane_direction"]},{"name":"branch_1","expected":"compliant","narrative":"The car stands still, loading, on the signposted one-way roadway with its body pointing against the designated direction. {"node_id":"NRS_484B_223_1b","law_refs":["NRS-484B-223-1b"],"subject":{"binder":"v","class_elements":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"]},"segmentation":[{"id":"s1","text":"If a highway has two or more clearly marked lanes for traffic traveling in one direction,","role":"trigger"},{"id":"s2","text":"vehicles must:","role":"subject"},{"id":"s3","text":"Not be moved from that lane","role":"obligation"},{"id":"s4","text":"until the driver has given the appropriate turn signal","role":"condition"},{"id":"s5","text":"and ascertained that such movement can be made with highway” is st.highway, “the entire width between the boundary lines of every way dedicated to a public authority when any part of the way is open to the use of the public for purposes of vehicular traffic”, DEF-NRS-484A-095's words, anchored to the subject by rel.occupies and tied to the lanes by st.on_way, “the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on — a lane, roadway, shoulder …”. “two or more … lanes … traveling in one direction” is st.lane, “a longitudinal strip of roadway for one line of vehicles”, with st.lane_adjacency, which carries “lane ordinal within the carriageway and the count of lanes in that direction”, the count the words require, and st.lane_direction, “direction of travel designated for a structure a vehicle travels in”, which fixes that the lanes counted are those of one direction — the direction of the lane the subject occupies. st.lane's exclusion “not a stand-in for a half of the roadway or a lateral position within a lane” is respected: the rule reads the mapped lanes and their count, not an offset from the edge. “clearly marked” is read through st.lane_marking, “per side of a lane: type ∈ {none, broken, solid, double_solid, solid_broken, dotted, curb}, colour …”: a lane marked on the side the movement crosses carries a marking of a type other than none, and the clarity of the paint is not modelled (narrowing on this span). “traffic” claims its admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic, which fixes whose travel the lanes are for. The literal two is the law's own figure."},{"span":"s2","atoms":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"],"derived":[],"justification":"“vehicles” is the term DEF-NRS-484A-320 defines and the run admits as DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, so the span claims ru.aggregate with that id and never the classes it covers."},{"span":"s3","atoms":["st.lane","rel.occupies"],"derived":["drv.lane.lane_change"],"justification":"“moved from that lane” is a manoeuvre and maps to a concept: drv.lane.lane_change states that the road user's footprint overlapped the region at the observation before and that at the observation it either no longer overlaps it or overlaps a lane adjacent to it that it did not overlap before, built on rel.occupies, “a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region”, and st.lane_adjacency, “left / right neighbouring lane of the same direction”. The concept takes the lane as a region formal, so the lane it reads is the one “that lane” singles out — the marked lane the trigger binds for the subject — and not any lane of the scene. st.lane is the kind that region argument admits and rel.occupies the anchor; the heading change is not read, since the words forbid the movement out of the lane and not a turn."},{"span":"s4","atoms":["sig.turn_indicator","sig.hand_signal","st.lane_adjacency","st.lane"],"derived":[],"justification":"“the appropriate turn signal” is the signal the vehicle emits: sig.turn_indicator is “the turn indicator state ∈ {off, left, right}: neither indicator lit, or the left or the right one”, and sig.hand_signal “a driver's or rider's arm signal; meaning ∈ {no_signal, left, right, stop_or_slow, re_enter}”, which is the other way the same indication is given and which the law's own scheme admits. sig.turn_indicator's exclusion “not a stand-in for the turn or lane change itself — the indicator is the signal that precedes a manoeuvre, judged separately from it” is exactly the separation these words make, the manoeuvre being s3's concept. Which indication is the appropriate one is st.lane_adjacency, the “left / right neighbouring lane of the same direction”: the appropriate signal is left where the lane the vehicle moves into is the left neighbour of the lane it leaves and right where it is the right neighbour; st.lane is the kind of both regions. “the driver has given” is read through the signal the vehicle shows (narrowing on this span)."}],"operationalizations":[{"span":"s5","standard":"ascertained that such movement can be made with safety","concepts":["rel.surface_gap","kin.speed","prim.closest_approach_within","prim.closest_approach_distance","rel.occupies","st.lane","ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic","drv.lane.lane_change"],"params":["p.lane_change_entry_headway_time","p.lane_change_min_clearance","p.lane_change_conflict_horizon"],"convention":"Gap-acceptance and conflict-avoidance convention (critical lane-change gap, with a closest-approach test over a conflict horizon). The movement can be made with safety at the observation of the change where, for every road user of DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic other than the subject that occupies the lane the subject moves into (rel.occupies with st.lane) or lies alongside the subject: the longitudinal component of rel.surface_gap, “distance between the nearest points of two bodies … its longitudinal and lateral components”, is at least p.lane_change_min_clearance + p.lane_change_entry_headway_time × the greater of the two kin.speed readings, so the required clearance grows with the speed of the faster of the pair; and the two do not close to less than p.lane_change_min_clearance within the horizon, which prim.closest_approach_within, “under constant velocities, the centres of two road users approach each other at some time between the observation and the horizon”, and prim.closest_approach_distance, “the centre distance at that closest approach”, decide over p.lane_change_conflict_horizon. drv.lane.lane_change fixes the observation and the lane the test is made for. The clearance and the horizon are parameters of the reading; the words state no figure.","surrogate":false}],"assumptions":[],"intentions":[],"compositions":[],"residues":[],"binders":[{"name":"v","class_elements":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"]}],"applicability":"The bound road user is a vehicle of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle whose footprint overlaps a marked lane L of a highway, where the count of lanes in L's direction of travel on that carriageway is at least the literal two and L carries a marking on the side the movement crosses. L is the lane the words single out as “that lane”: the obligation binds it again with the whole of that selection — a lane of the same highway, in a direction with at least two lanes, marked, and occupied by the subject at the observation before the movement — and the duty is written for every such lane the subject occupies, since the words require it of each.","obligation":"At each observation at which the subject moves out of such a lane L (drv.lane.lane_change for the subject and L), the appropriate turn signal must have been given for that movement and the movement must be one that can be made with safety on the bound of s5. The signal is appropriate where sig.turn_indicator shows left, or sig.hand_signal means left, while the lane entered is the left neighbour of L, and shows or means right while it is the right neighbour; where the lane entered is no neighbour of L in L's direction, either indication given for the side the body moves towards counts. It has been given where the appropriate indication holds at the observation of the movement or at some observation in the window of p.turn_signal_advance_window behind it. Where the movement is made with no appropriate indication in that window, or where the clearances of s5 are not met at the observation of the movement, the duty is violated; where the indicator, the hand signal, a gap or a speed the bound reads is unobserved, or the window behind reaches past the start of the recording with no indication in the part observed, the duty is unknown. Where the subject does not move out of the lane, the duty is complied with.","params":["p.turn_signal_advance_window","p.lane_change_entry_headway_time","p.lane_change_min_clearance","p.lane_change_conflict_horizon"],"narrowings":[{"span":"s1","why":"“clearly marked lanes” is read as the lanes the map represents with a marking of a type other than none on the side the movement crosses. The reading relaxes nothing about which lanes are counted or which lane the duty is owed from.","kind":"observable_reading","category":"status"},{"span":"s2","why":"“vehicles must” is read as the vehicle's controlled motion: who or what controls a road user is not observable, and the ontology reads a duty stated of a vehicle through that vehicle's conduct.","kind":"observable_reading","category":"agency"},{"span":"s4","why":"“the driver has given” is read as the signal the vehicle shows: who gives the indication is not observable, and the ontology reads such words through the observable feature — the indicator's state or the arm signal's meaning — whoever or whatever operates it.","kind":"observable_reading","category":"agency"},{"span":"s3","why":"“until the driver has given the appropriate turn signal” states no duration, so the look-back is bounded by p.turn_signal_advance_window: an indication counts as given for the movement where it holds at the observation of the movement or at some observation within that window behind it. The purpose of the bound is to give the search a stated extent, as a fixed, parameterized recognition bound rather than a search over the whole recording; a window that reaches past the start of the recording leaves the duty unknown rather than violated, so the bound never turns a signal the trace does not cover into a breach.","kind":"reading"},{"span":"s5","why":"“ascertained that such movement can be made with safety” is read through the outcome the duty secures: the movement made with the clearances the reading sets. {"node_id":"NRS_484B_227_1_o1","law_refs":["NRS-484B-227-1"],"subject":{"binder":"v","class_elements":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"]},"segmentation":[{"id":"s1","text":"Every vehicle driven upon a divided highway","role":"subject"},{"id":"s2","text":"must be driven only upon the right-hand roadway","role":"obligation"},{"id":"s3","text":"and must not be driven over, across or within any dividing space, barrier or section or make any left turn, semicircular turn or U-turn,","role":"sibling"},{"id":"s4","text":"except through an opening in the barrier or dividing section or space or at a crossover or intersection established by a public authority.","role":"exception"}],"elements":[{"span":"s1","atoms":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle","st.highway","st.roadway","st.median_or_divider","st.on_way","rel.occupies"],"derived":["drv.motion.standstill"],"justification":"“vehicle” is the term DEF-NRS-484A-320 defines and the run admits as DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed as ru.aggregate with that id. “a divided highway” is DEF-NRS-484A-070, “a highway divided into two or more roadways by means of a physical barrier or dividing section, constructed so as to impede the conflict of vehicular traffic traveling in opposite directions”: st.highway is the way, st.median_or_divider the “physical barrier or dividing section between roadways; opening attribute where a crossover exists”, st.roadway “the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic, excluding shoulder; separate roadways of a divided highway are separate” — which carries the definition's division into roadways in the atom's own words — and st.on_way, “the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on”, is what makes the divider and the roadways parts of one way. rel.occupies anchors the way to the subject. “driven upon” is read through controlled motion (narrowing on this span): the negation of drv.motion.standstill states that the vehicle is moving."},{"span":"s2","atoms":["st.roadway","rel.occupies","st.lane_direction","st.median_or_divider","st.on_way","prim.region_lateral_offset"],"derived":["drv.position.direction_component"],"justification":"“the right-hand roadway” of a divided highway is the roadway of that way whose designated direction of travel is the one the vehicle travels in and which has the dividing section on its left. st.roadway is the atom for the roadway, with “separate roadways of a divided highway are separate” in its own contract, anchored by rel.occupies; st.on_way ties the roadway to the same way as the divider. The direction is read by drv.position.direction_component, the component of the vehicle's velocity along st.lane_direction, “direction of travel designated for a structure a vehicle travels in — … a roadway, one-way roadway or shoulder”. {"concept_id":"drv.motion.standstill","kind":"formula","contract":"The road user is motionless at the observation: the magnitude of its velocity is at most the speed tolerance, a speed the caller sets, so that a sampled reading at or below it is read as no movement at all. {"concept_id":"drv.interaction.following","kind":"formula","contract":"Road user a is following road user b at the observation: b is ahead of a in the same lane along that lane's direction of travel, and the two bodies' headings are aligned within the same-direction tolerance, a cosine the caller sets. {"concept_id":"drv.interaction.overtaking","kind":"formula","contract":"Road user a is passing road user b at the observation: the two headings are aligned within the same-direction tolerance, a's speed exceeds b's by at least the speed excess the caller sets, and either the two bodies' projections on a's heading overlap — a is drawing level with b — or b is still ahead of a in the same lane. {"concept_id":"drv.interaction.vehicle_file","kind":"formula","contract":"Road user u is one of a file of road users travelling one behind another at the observation: counting u itself, at least the minimum member count of road users have their heading aligned with u's within the same-direction tolerance, lie ahead of or behind u in the same lane, and are within the file reach of u, a distance the caller sets measured between the nearest points of the bodies. It is a relation of place, direction and spacing at the observation. It says nothing of why the road users travel together, of a common destination or origin, of an organizer, or of their speed: a caller that means a moving file states the motion itself. Not a stand-in for: a chain each of whose consecutive spaces is bounded — the reach is measured from u to each member, so a long file is read through the membership of each road user in turn — the class of the members, which the caller states, or a towed combination, which is one road user drawn by another.","definition":null,"args":[{"name":"u","sort":"track"}],"params":[{"name":"min_member_count","unit":"1","meaning":"the number of road users, u included, at which the group is read as a file rather than as road users happening to follow one another"},{"name":"file_reach","unit":"m","meaning":"the distance between the nearest points of two bodies within which another road user is read as travelling with u in the same file"},{"name":"same_direction_tolerance","unit":"1","meaning":"the cosine of the largest angle between two headings still read as the same direction, a ratio between minus one and one"}],"elements":[{"span":"have their heading aligned with u's within the same-direction tolerance","atoms":["rel.same_direction"],"concepts":[],"justification":"rel.same_direction is “headings aligned: the cosine of the angle between the headings is above its tolerance”, the relation this clause states, the tolerance being the atom's own parameter."},{"span":"lie ahead of or behind u in the same lane","atoms":["rel.ahead_behind_in_lane"],"concepts":[],"justification":"rel.ahead_behind_in_lane is “a is ahead of / behind b in the same lane, along the lane direction”, which is the one-behind-another arrangement this clause states; rel.bearing is not read, giving only a direction and not an in-lane order."},{"span":"are within the file reach of u, a distance … measured between the nearest points of the bodies","atoms":["rel.surface_gap"],"concepts":[],"justification":"rel.surface_gap is the “distance between the nearest points of two bodies, each body's footprint read with its own heading and extent”, which is the spacing this clause bounds; rel.centre_distance is excluded by its own contract as “not a stand-in for a clearance between bodies”."}],"residues":[],"literals":[],"scenarios":[{"name":"holds","expected":"compliant","narrative":"Five cars run in file in one lane of a rural highway, each within 20 m of the next and all headings aligned: each of them, counting itself, has at least three members of the group within the reach, ahead of or behind it in the lane.","masked":[]},{"name":"fails","expected":"violated","narrative":"One car runs alone in that lane with the nearest other road user 400 m ahead: the minimum member count is not reached within the reach.","masked":[]},{"name":"blind","expected":"unknown","narrative":"The five cars with the source declaring the gap between bodies absent: how far apart the members are, and so how many lie within the reach, cannot be read.","masked":["rel.surface_gap"]}],"used_by":["NRS_484B_127_3"],"supersedes":null}
{"concept_id":"drv.position.direction_component","kind":"quantity","contract":"The component, in metres per second, of a road user's velocity along the designated direction of travel of a structure region: positive where the road user moves with that direction, negative where it moves against it, and near zero where it stands or moves across it. The quantity is geometric only: it does not state that the road user is on the region, that the region is the one a law names, or how far the road user is from it, and a caller states those with its own relations. Unknown where the road user's velocity is absent and where the region carries no designated direction — a centre turn lane carries none, and a place no carrier covers has none. Not a stand-in for: the direction the body points, which a road user may hold while moving another way, the road user's speed, which is unsigned, or an angle between the two directions.","definition":null,"args":[{"name":"u","sort":"track"},{"name":"r","sort":"region"}],"params":[],"elements":[{"span":"a road user's velocity","atoms":["kin.velocity"],"concepts":[],"justification":"kin.velocity is the “velocity vector” of a road user, in m/s in the world frame, whose components are what this quantity projects; {"concept_id":"drv.lane.lane_change","kind":"formula","contract":"The road user crosses out of a structure region at the observation: its footprint overlapped the region at the observation before, and at the observation it either no longer overlaps that region or overlaps a lane neighbouring it in the same direction of travel which it did not overlap at the observation before. Not a stand-in for: a turn, since no heading change is read, a signal or a declared intention, a movement that stays within the region however far across it, the completion of a movement into the neighbouring region, or the direction or side the crossing is made towards, which a caller reads from the regions themselves.","definition":null,"args":[{"name":"u","sort":"track"},{"name":"r","sort":"region"}],"params":[],"elements":[{"span":"its footprint overlapped the region at the observation before","atoms":["rel.occupies"],"concepts":[],"justification":"rel.occupies is “a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region (roadway, shoulder, sidewalk, intersection, crosswalk …)”, which is the occupancy this clause reads, taken at the previous observation by the formula language's own past reading; the neighbour is a region of kind st.lane, “a longitudinal strip of roadway for one line of vehicles”, which the body's quantifier ranges over, and rel.occupies is the overlap of the footprint with it."}],"residues":[],"literals":[],"scenarios":[{"name":"holds","expected":"compliant","narrative":"A car running in the middle lane of a three-lane carriageway reaches the left-hand lane: at the observation before, its footprint overlapped the middle lane alone; at the observation it overlaps the left-hand lane as well.","masked":[]},{"name":"fails","expected":"violated","narrative":"The same car drifts to the left within the middle lane and back again: its footprint overlaps the middle lane and no neighbouring lane at every observation.","masked":[]},{"name":"blind","expected":"unknown","narrative":"The same movement with the source declaring the occupancy of regions by road users absent: whether the footprint overlapped the lane before and the neighbour now cannot be read.","masked":["rel.occupies"]}],"used_by":["NRS_484B_223_1b"],"supersedes":null}
{"concept_id":"drv.motion.left_turn","kind":"formula","contract":"The road user has turned to the left: counting from the onset of the turning — the observation at which its rate of change of heading to the left first rose above the onset yaw rate, a rate the caller sets — the heading change accumulated since that onset reaches at least the turn angle, a size the caller sets, to the left. The concept becomes true at the observation at which that angle is first reached and stays true at the later observations at which the accumulated change still holds it, until a later onset starts the count again; the integration is bounded by the heading step, the largest interval between consecutive observations it may integrate across. It states the turning of the body only: no place, no lane, no way and no destination. Not a stand-in for: a signal or a declared intention, a steering input, the curvature of the road — a body yaws on a straight road whenever it manoeuvres — a lane change, or a reversal of the direction of travel, which is a larger angle and has its own concept.","definition":null,"args":[{"name":"u","sort":"track"}],"params":[{"name":"heading_step","unit":"ms","meaning":"the largest interval between two consecutive observations the heading integration may cross, the sampling standard of the acquisition profile"},{"name":"onset_yaw_rate","unit":"deg/s","meaning":"the rate of change of heading above which the body is read as beginning to turn rather than running straight, which fixes the observed onset the heading change is counted from"},{"name":"turn_angle","unit":"deg","meaning":"the accumulated heading change at which a turn to the left is recognized"}],"act":{"boundary":"event","onset":"the observation at which its rate of change of heading to the left first rose above the onset yaw rate","recognition":"the observation at which the heading change accumulated since that onset reaches at least the turn angle","extent":"the later observations at which the accumulated change still holds the turn angle, until a later onset starts the count again","history":"the onset must be observed, with the rate of change of heading known at every observation from the one before it onwards and no interval between consecutive observations longer than the heading step; where no such onset is observed within the recording, or a yaw rate since it is missing, the concept is unknown and never false"},"elements":[{"span":"its rate of change of heading to the left first rose above the onset yaw rate","atoms":["kin.yaw_rate"],"concepts":[],"justification":"kin.yaw_rate is the “rate of change of heading, positive when the heading turns to the left (counter-clockwise)”, in deg/s, which is the quantity whose rise marks the onset; its exclusion “not a stand-in for road curvature — a vehicle yaws on a straight road whenever it manoeuvres” does not apply, because the body's yaw and not the road's bend is what the contract reads."},{"span":"the heading change accumulated since that onset","atoms":["kin.yaw_rate"],"concepts":[],"justification":"The accumulated heading change since an observed onset is integrated from the same atom by the formula language's own construct, which the ontology describes as “the signed heading change of a road user since a formula last became true, integrated from kin.yaw_rate with a step bound”; {"concept_id":"drv.motion.u_turn","kind":"formula","contract":"The road user's direction of travel upon a way has reversed: counting from the onset of the manoeuvre — the observation at which the magnitude of its rate of change of heading first rose above the onset yaw rate, a rate the caller sets — the magnitude of the heading change accumulated since that onset reaches at least the reversal angle, a size the caller sets below a half turn, while the road user's footprint overlaps a way. The definition this contract carries is the turning of a vehicle upon a highway “so as to proceed in the opposite direction”, “whether accomplished by one continuous movement or not”, so halts, rearward movements and steering the other way between the onset and the reversal do not end the manoeuvre, and the count runs on until the angle is reached or a later onset starts it again; the integration is bounded by the heading step, the largest interval between consecutive observations it may integrate across. The reversal angle is the contract's own magnitude, the bound within which a sampled heading change is read as the opposite direction. Not a stand-in for: a turn through a smaller angle, which has its own concept, a turn into another way, travel against a designated direction of travel, a reversing movement, or a signal or a declared intention.","definition":"DEF-NRS-484B-077","args":[{"name":"u","sort":"track"}],"params":[{"name":"heading_step","unit":"ms","meaning":"the largest interval between two consecutive observations the heading integration may cross, the sampling standard of the acquisition profile"},{"name":"onset_yaw_rate","unit":"deg/s","meaning":"the rate of change of heading above which the body is read as beginning to turn rather than running straight, which fixes the observed onset the heading change is counted from"},{"name":"reversal_angle","unit":"deg","meaning":"the accumulated heading change at which the definition's proceeding in the opposite direction is recognized; it is set below a half turn so that a reversal sampled coarsely or made on a skewed way is still recognized"}],"act":{"boundary":"event","onset":"the observation at which the magnitude of its rate of change of heading first rose above the onset yaw rate","recognition":"the observation at which the magnitude of the heading change accumulated since that onset reaches at least the reversal angle","extent":"the later observations at which the accumulated change still holds the reversal angle, until a later onset starts the count again","history":"the onset must be observed, with the rate of change of heading known at every observation from the one before it onwards and no interval between consecutive observations longer than the heading step; its exclusion of road curvature does not apply, the body's yaw being what is read."},{"span":"the magnitude of the heading change accumulated since that onset","atoms":["kin.yaw_rate"],"concepts":[],"justification":"The accumulated heading change since an observed onset is integrated from the same atom by the formula language's own construct, “the signed heading change of a road user since a formula last became true, integrated from kin.yaw_rate with a step bound”; the concept is written for any road user and adds no class of its own."}],"literals":[],"scenarios":[{"name":"holds","expected":"compliant","narrative":"A car on a city street swings left across the way, halts to let a vehicle pass, reverses a metre and completes the swing: from the onset of the turning the accumulated heading change reaches about a hundred and seventy degrees while its footprint overlaps the way.","masked":[]},{"name":"fails","expected":"violated","narrative":"The same car turns left into a side street: the accumulated heading change since the onset peaks at about ninety degrees and never reaches the reversal angle.","masked":[]},{"name":"blind","expected":"unknown","narrative":"The car is already mid-turn at the first observation of the recording, so no onset is observed with the yaw rate known at every observation since: whether the direction reversed cannot be read.","masked":["kin.yaw_rate"]}],"used_by":["NRS_484B_227_1_o2"],"supersedes":null,"differs_from":{"concept":"drv.motion.left_turn","why":"Both take one road user and read the same atom, but they recognize different manoeuvres and decide differently for the same motion: the left turn is recognized at a smaller angle to the left alone, while this concept reads the magnitude of the accumulated change, so it holds for a reversal to either hand and is false of an ordinary junction turn that the left-turn concept recognizes."}}

lines: -{"node_id":"NRS_484A_450_2","law_refs":["NRS-484A-450-2"],"subject":{"binder":"v","class_elements":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"]},"segmentation":[{"id":"s1","text":"Every driver of a vehicle","role":"subject"},{"id":"s2","text":"approaching a stop intersection indicated by a stop sign","role":"trigger"},{"id":"s3","text":"shall stop before entering the crosswalk on the near side of the intersection or, if there is no crosswalk, shall stop at a clearly marked stop line, or if none, then at the point nearest the intersecting highway","role":"obligation"},{"id":"s4","text":"where the driver has a view of approaching traffic on the intersecting highway","role":"standard"},{"id":"s5","text":"before entering the intersection.","role":"condition"}],"elements":[{"span":"s1","atoms":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"],"derived":[],"justification":"“vehicle” is the term DEF-NRS-484A-320 defines and the run admits as the aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, so the span claims ru.aggregate with that id: the atom is “membership of a legal aggregate: the atom's literal argument is an aggregate id”, true where the road user carries an included class, unknown where an included or unresolved class it might carry is unobserved. Its exclusion “not a stand-in for a named road-user class” does not apply, because the admitted aggregate is claimed as the aggregate and never replaced by a class atom; its exclusion of “a relational role such as who drives or controls a vehicle” is respected by reading “driver” through the vehicle's controlled motion (narrowing on this span) rather than as a member of the aggregate."},{"span":"s2","atoms":["st.intersection","st.travel_region","rel.occupies","st.lane_enters","dev.stop_sign","dev.governs"],"derived":[],"justification":"The approach is read as the ontology's section on an act due at a place before an event states it: “a road user's approach to an intersection is a carrier it occupies (rel.occupies) whose entrance end is that intersection”. st.intersection is “the region where two roadways meet, bounded by the prolongation of their edges”, the region the words call the intersection; st.travel_region is the kind the carrier quantifier ranges over, “the union of the kinds a device can govern … a lane and the kinds that refine it, a bicycle lane or path, a roadway and the kinds that refine it, a shoulder, or an intersection”, which is exactly the set of carriers st.lane_enters admits, so each region argument of the claimed relations has a claimed kind; st.lane_enters is “the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end”, and its clause “it is entry topology: it is decided where the source records it … never inferred from distance, overlap or a road user's velocity” is why approaching is not read from heading or closing speed. dev.stop_sign is the “regulatory sign requiring a full halt”, the sign the words name, and dev.governs, “the travel regions whose traffic the device controls … or an intersection”, ties it to the carrier the vehicle approaches through, as the ontology directs (“the mark that governs that approach is one the source records as marking that carrier”); dev.governs's exclusion “not a stand-in for a position” does not apply, because the place of the halt is read from the crosswalk, the stop line or the view point in s3 and never from where the sign stands. rel.occupies is “a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region”, the anchor that makes the carrier the subject's own."},{"span":"s3","atoms":["st.crosswalk","st.stop_line","st.travel_region","st.entrance_of","st.lane_direction","st.region_geometry","rel.occupies","st.intersection","st.highway","st.on_way","prim.region_offset_along"],"derived":["drv.motion.standstill"],"justification":"“shall stop” is the act: drv.motion.standstill carries the posted definition DEF-NRS-484A-255, “complete cessation from movement”, as a motion state at an observation, with the speed tolerance the sampling leaves to the observer. The first place is the crosswalk “on the near side of the intersection”: st.crosswalk is the “marked crossing, or the unmarked prolongation of sidewalks at an intersection”, and which crossing is the near one is st.entrance_of, “the carrier whose entrance into an intersection a stop line or a crosswalk marks — exactly that carrier's entrance, the line or crossing a vehicle approaching through that carrier halts at or before”, read on the same carrier st.lane_enters relates to the intersection; st.entrance_of's exclusion “not a stand-in for distance to the line” is why nearness never selects the crossing. The second place is st.stop_line, “the transverse line marking where vehicles halt for a device”, taken where the crosswalk's observed list of entrances excludes the carrier, as st.entrance_of's completeness clause permits. {"concept_id":"drv.interaction.vehicle_file","kind":"formula","contract":"Road user u is one of a file of road users travelling one behind another at the observation: counting u itself, at least the minimum member count of road users have their heading aligned with u's within the same-direction tolerance, lie ahead of or behind u in the same lane, and are within the file reach of u, a distance the caller sets measured between the nearest points of the bodies. {"concept_id":"drv.motion.left_turn","kind":"formula","contract":"The road user has turned to the left: counting from the onset of the turning — the observation at which its rate of change of heading to the left first rose above the onset yaw rate, a rate the caller sets — the heading change accumulated since that onset reaches at least the turn angle, a size the caller sets, to the left. lines: {"node_id":"NRS_484A_450_2","law_refs":["NRS-484A-450-2"],"subject":{"binder":"v","class_elements":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"]},"segmentation":[{"id":"s1","text":"Every driver of a vehicle","role":"subject"},{"id":"s2","text":"approaching a stop intersection indicated by a stop sign","role":"trigger"},{"id":"s3","text":"shall stop before entering the crosswalk on the near side of the intersection or, if there is no crosswalk, shall stop at a clearly marked stop line, or if none, then at the point nearest the intersecting highway","role":"obligation"},{"id":"s4","text":"where the driver has a view of approaching traffic on the intersecting highway","role":"standard"},{"id":"s5","text":"before entering the intersection.","role":"condition"}],"elements":[{"span":"s1","atoms":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"],"derived":[],"justification":"“vehicle” is the term DEF-NRS-484A-320 defines and the run admits as the aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, so the span claims ru.aggregate with that id: the atom is “membership of a legal aggregate: the atom's literal argument is an aggregate id”, true where the road user carries an included class, unknown where an included or unresolved class it might carry is unobserved. Its exclusion “not a stand-in for a named road-user class” does not apply, because the admitted aggregate is claimed as the aggregate and never replaced by a class atom; its exclusion of “a relational role such as who drives or controls a vehicle” is respected by reading “driver” through the vehicle's controlled motion (narrowing on this span) rather than as a member of the aggregate."},{"span":"s2","atoms":["st.intersection","st.travel_region","rel.occupies","st.lane_enters","dev.stop_sign","dev.governs"],"derived":[],"justification":"The approach is read as the ontology's section on an act due at a place before an event states it: “a road user's approach to an intersection is a carrier it occupies (rel.occupies) whose entrance end is that intersection”. st.intersection is “the region where two roadways meet, bounded by the prolongation of their edges”, the region the words call the intersection; st.travel_region is the kind the carrier quantifier ranges over, “the union of the kinds a device can govern … a lane and the kinds that refine it, a bicycle lane or path, a roadway and the kinds that refine it, a shoulder, or an intersection”, which is exactly the set of carriers st.lane_enters admits, so each region argument of the claimed relations has a claimed kind; st.lane_enters is “the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end”, and its clause “it is entry topology: it is decided where the source records it … never inferred from distance, overlap or a road user's velocity” is why approaching is not read from heading or closing speed. dev.stop_sign is the “regulatory sign requiring a full halt”, the sign the words name, and dev.governs, “the travel regions whose traffic the device controls … or an intersection”, ties it to the carrier the vehicle approaches through, as the ontology directs (“the mark that governs that approach is one the source records as marking that carrier”); dev.governs's exclusion “not a stand-in for a position” does not apply, because the place of the halt is read from the crosswalk, the stop line or the view point in s3 and never from where the sign stands. rel.occupies is “a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region”, the anchor that makes the carrier the subject's own."},{"span":"s3","atoms":["st.crosswalk","st.stop_line","st.travel_region","st.entrance_of","st.lane_direction","st.region_geometry","rel.occupies","st.intersection","st.highway","st.on_way","prim.region_offset_along"],"derived":["drv.motion.standstill"],"justification":"“shall stop” is the act: drv.motion.standstill carries the posted definition DEF-NRS-484A-255, “complete cessation from movement”, as a motion state at an observation, with the speed tolerance the sampling leaves to the observer. The first place is the crosswalk “on the near side of the intersection”: st.crosswalk is the “marked crossing, or the unmarked prolongation of sidewalks at an intersection”, and which crossing is the near one is st.entrance_of, “the carrier whose entrance into an intersection a stop line or a crosswalk marks — exactly that carrier's entrance, the line or crossing a vehicle approaching through that carrier halts at or before”, read on the same carrier st.lane_enters relates to the intersection; st.entrance_of's exclusion “not a stand-in for distance to the line” is why nearness never selects the crossing. The second place is st.stop_line, “the transverse line marking where vehicles halt for a device”, taken where the crosswalk's observed list of entrances excludes the carrier, as st.entrance_of's completeness clause permits. The third is the point nearest the intersecting highway, read on the carrier (st.travel_region) against the way the junction lies on: st.highway is “the entire width between the boundary lines of every way”, st.on_way “the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on — … an intersection lies on every way that meets there”, so the intersecting highway is a way the intersection lies on other than the one the carrier lies on. lines: {"node_id":"NRS_484A_450_2","law_refs":["NRS-484A-450-2"],"subject":{"binder":"v","class_elements":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"]},"segmentation":[{"id":"s1","text":"Every driver of a vehicle","role":"subject"},{"id":"s2","text":"approaching a stop intersection indicated by a stop sign","role":"trigger"},{"id":"s3","text":"shall stop before entering the crosswalk on the near side of the intersection or, if there is no crosswalk, shall stop at a clearly marked stop line, or if none, then at the point nearest the intersecting highway","role":"obligation"},{"id":"s4","text":"where the driver has a view of approaching traffic on the intersecting highway","role":"standard"},{"id":"s5","text":"before entering the intersection.","role":"condition"}],"elements":[{"span":"s1","atoms":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"],"derived":[],"justification":"“vehicle” is the term DEF-NRS-484A-320 defines and the run admits as the aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, so the span claims ru.aggregate with that id: the atom is “membership of a legal aggregate: the atom's literal argument is an aggregate id”, true where the road user carries an included class, unknown where an included or unresolved class it might carry is unobserved. Its exclusion “not a stand-in for a named road-user class” does not apply, because the admitted aggregate is claimed as the aggregate and never replaced by a class atom; its exclusion of “a relational role such as who drives or controls a vehicle” is respected by reading “driver” through the vehicle's controlled motion (narrowing on this span) rather than as a member of the aggregate."},{"span":"s2","atoms":["st.intersection","st.travel_region","rel.occupies","st.lane_enters","dev.stop_sign","dev.governs"],"derived":[],"justification":"The approach is read as the ontology's section on an act due at a place before an event states it: “a road user's approach to an intersection is a carrier it occupies (rel.occupies) whose entrance end is that intersection”. st.intersection is “the region where two roadways meet, bounded by the prolongation of their edges”, the region the words call the intersection; st.travel_region is the kind the carrier quantifier ranges over, “the union of the kinds a device can govern … a lane and the kinds that refine it, a bicycle lane or path, a roadway and the kinds that refine it, a shoulder, or an intersection”, which is exactly the set of carriers st.lane_enters admits, so each region argument of the claimed relations has a claimed kind; st.lane_enters is “the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end”, and its clause “it is entry topology: it is decided where the source records it … never inferred from distance, overlap or a road user's velocity” is why approaching is not read from heading or closing speed. dev.stop_sign is the “regulatory sign requiring a full halt”, the sign the words name, and dev.governs, “the travel regions whose traffic the device controls … or an intersection”, ties it to the carrier the vehicle approaches through, as the ontology directs (“the mark that governs that approach is one the source records as marking that carrier”); dev.governs's exclusion “not a stand-in for a position” does not apply, because the place of the halt is read from the crosswalk, the stop line or the view point in s3 and never from where the sign stands. rel.occupies is “a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region”, the anchor that makes the carrier the subject's own."},{"span":"s3","atoms":["st.crosswalk","st.stop_line","st.travel_region","st.entrance_of","st.lane_direction","st.region_geometry","rel.occupies","st.intersection","st.highway","st.on_way","prim.region_offset_along"],"derived":["drv.motion.standstill"],"justification":"“shall stop” is the act: drv.motion.standstill carries the posted definition DEF-NRS-484A-255, “complete cessation from movement”, as a motion state at an observation, with the speed tolerance the sampling leaves to the observer. The first place is the crosswalk “on the near side of the intersection”: st.crosswalk is the “marked crossing, or the unmarked prolongation of sidewalks at an intersection”, and which crossing is the near one is st.entrance_of, “the carrier whose entrance into an intersection a stop line or a crosswalk marks — exactly that carrier's entrance, the line or crossing a vehicle approaching through that carrier halts at or before”, read on the same carrier st.lane_enters relates to the intersection; st.entrance_of's exclusion “not a stand-in for distance to the line” is why nearness never selects the crossing. The second place is st.stop_line, “the transverse line marking where vehicles halt for a device”, taken where the crosswalk's observed list of entrances excludes the carrier, as st.entrance_of's completeness clause permits. The third is the point nearest the intersecting highway, read on the carrier (st.travel_region) against the way the junction lies on: st.highway is “the entire width between the boundary lines of every way”, st.on_way “the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on — … an intersection lies on every way that meets there”, so the intersecting highway is a way the intersection lies on other than the one the carrier lies on. That the halt is at the place and on the near side of it is st.region_geometry, “the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it”, within p.stop_point_tolerance, with the side taken from prim.region_offset_along, “the signed distance … measured along a carrier's designated direction (st.lane_direction)”, whose sign gives the side as the ontology requires (“the side of the mark is read along that carrier's designated direction … never along the road user's heading”); the primitive's own inputs are not claimed again beyond st.lane_direction and st.region_geometry, which the rule also reads on their own for the direction and for the distance, since prim.region_offset_along “is a geometric quantity only … a distance to the region is read from st.region_geometry, never from this value”. rel.occupies excludes a halt whose footprint already overlaps the crossing or the junction, which the words place the halt before, and st.intersection is the region that entry concerns."},{"span":"s5","atoms":["st.intersection","rel.occupies"],"derived":[],"justification":"“before entering the intersection” is the event the duty is owed before: the observation at which the vehicle's footprint first overlaps the intersection region. rel.occupies is “a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region (… intersection …)” and st.intersection the region itself; st.intersection's exclusion “not a stand-in for a crosswalk or a stop line — a stop before the crossing is earlier than a stop before the intersection” is precisely the distinction kept here, the crossing being the place of the act in s3 and the junction the event in this span."}],"operationalizations":[{"span":"s4","standard":"where the driver has a view of approaching traffic on the intersecting highway","concepts":["st.sight_along_way","st.highway","st.on_way","st.intersection","rel.visible","ru.aggregate","st.travel_region","rel.occupies"],"params":["p.intersecting_way_view_distance"],"convention":"Intersection sight-distance convention (AASHTO Green Book intersection sight distance, the departure-sight-triangle cases): a driver halted at the stopping point must be able to see along the major way at least the distance an approaching vehicle travels in the time needed to judge a gap and clear the junction. The point is adequate where st.sight_along_way, “the distance along a way, in each direction from the point of that way nearest a road user, within which another vehicle on that way could be seen from the road user's eye at the observation … the smaller of the two directions”, taken for the intersecting highway the junction lies on (st.highway with st.on_way and st.intersection), is at least p.intersecting_way_view_distance, and where a road user that is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic is on that way approaching the junction, that road user is visible from the vehicle (rel.visible, “b is visible from a: an unobstructed line of sight”). The aggregate fixes whose approach counts as the traffic to be seen — “pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances … using any highway for purposes of travel” — and the sight atom carries the view itself, since rel.visible “is not a stand-in for … the sight distance of a place” and st.sight_along_way is “not a stand-in for … whether an actual road user is seen”: the two together read the span's words where a road user is present and where none is. p.intersecting_way_view_distance is the only magnitude, and it is the reading's, not the words'.","surrogate":false}],"assumptions":[],"intentions":[],"compositions":[],"residues":[],"binders":[{"name":"v","class_elements":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"]}],"applicability":"The bound road user is a vehicle of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle that occupies a travel region whose entrance end is an intersection (st.lane_enters on that carrier) and that a stop sign governs (dev.stop_sign with dev.governs on that same carrier), and that enters that intersection: the stop intersection indicated by a stop sign which it approaches. Where the sign's governance of the carrier is unobserved, whether the rule applies is unknown; where the source's complete record shows the sign governs no carrier the vehicle occupies, the rule does not apply.","obligation":"At each observation at which the vehicle's footprint first overlaps the intersection it approaches (the entry event: the rise of rel.occupies of the vehicle on the intersection X that the carrier it occupies runs into, st.lane_enters, read from this observation and the one before it), the vehicle must have been at a standstill (drv.motion.standstill with p.standstill_speed_tolerance) at some observation of the approach that leads to that entry, with its body at the place the words name. The place is read from the words in their order: first the crosswalk that marks the entrance of the carrier the vehicle approaches through (st.entrance_of on the same carrier st.lane_enters relates to X); where that crosswalk's entrances are observed, so that its list is complete, and exclude the carrier, the clearly marked stop line that marks it; where neither marks it, the point on the carrier nearest the intersecting highway at which the view of s4 is met. Where a mark's association with the carrier is not observed, whether that mark governs is unknown and the duty is unknown on that ground. A halt counts at the place where the distance from the vehicle's body to the mark (st.region_geometry) is within p.stop_point_tolerance and the mark lies ahead along the carrier's designated direction (the sign of prim.region_offset_along with st.lane_direction); the words placing the halt before the vehicle enters the crossing and the junction, a halt at which its footprint already overlaps that region (rel.occupies) is not at the place, and the tolerance applies outside that region only. The search for the halt runs back from the entry event and ends only at the start of that approach — the last observation before the event at which the vehicle, on a carrier the mark marks, is off the mark, short of it and farther from it than p.stop_point_tolerance — or at the previous entry of the same vehicle into the same intersection; nothing else ends it: not another junction or mark, not the start of the recording, not a first observation, not a distance travelled. Only an observed exit from the stopping zone upstream begins a new approach, so a vehicle that leaves the zone upstream and returns owes the halt again, while crossing the mark, moving on toward the junction, a change of carrier, a lateral move or a reverse within the zone begin none and lose no halt already made. Where the search finds the halt the duty is met; where it reaches either end without the halt the duty is violated; where it reaches neither end without finding it — the recording begins inside the stopping zone, the observation before the event does not show the vehicle's place relative to the mark through its carrier, or the speed that decides the standstill is unobserved — the duty is unknown. Each entry owes its own halt: a halt made before the previous entry of the same vehicle into the same intersection discharged that entry, not this one.","params":["p.standstill_speed_tolerance","p.stop_point_tolerance","p.intersecting_way_view_distance"],"narrowings":[{"span":"s1","why":"“Every driver of a vehicle” is read as the vehicle whose motion is controlled. Who or what controls a road user is not observable, and the ontology reads “drives”, “operates” and “the driver” through the vehicle's controlled motion, a vehicle moving on the road being taken to be driven, with the duty binding that vehicle's conduct whoever or whatever is at the controls.","kind":"observable_reading","category":"agency"},{"span":"s2","why":"“indicated by a stop sign” is read as the presence of a stop sign governing the approach. That a sign is official or posted by an authority is a legal status the ontology reads through the feature itself: the sign's presence on the road is the evidence of the designation the section's title speaks of.","kind":"observable_reading","category":"status"},{"span":"s3","why":"“a clearly marked stop line” is read as the stop line the scene represents. The ontology states this reading for exactly these words: the line's presence is the evidence, and the paint's clarity or wear is not modelled. The reading relaxes nothing about which place governs, the act or its timing.","kind":"observable_reading","category":"status"},{"span":"s3","why":"“the point nearest the intersecting highway where the driver has a view” is read as a point on the carrier the vehicle approaches through, rather than any point of the scene: the words single out the vehicle's own approach, and the place is read on the region the node binds. Among the points of that carrier at which the view of s4 is met, the duty is read as met by a halt at or before the nearest such point to the intersecting highway, within p.stop_point_tolerance of it, so a halt farther back on the same carrier that still meets the view is not a violation; this is the reading of “the point nearest … where the driver has a view”, which names a nearest point among those with a view and not a single surveyed spot.","kind":"reading"},{"span":"s4","why":"“the driver has a view of approaching traffic” is read as what could be seen along the intersecting way from where the vehicle stands, and as the visibility of a road user of the traffic aggregate that is there. What a driver perceived is not observable; the ontology directs that where the words offer observable evidence the rule reads it, “what was in an actual road user's line of sight is rel.visible; what could be seen from or at a place is st.sight_distance”, and st.sight_along_way is that quantity measured along the way for a road user at the observation.","kind":"observable_reading","category":"perception"}],"scenarios":[{"name":"forbid","expected":"violated","narrative":"A car runs along a marked lane that the source records as entering a four-way junction, and a stop sign governs that lane. A marked crosswalk is recorded as marking that lane's entrance. From the last observation at which the car is off the crossing, short of it and more than the stop-point tolerance from it, through to the observation at which its footprint first overlaps the junction, its speed never falls to the standstill tolerance: it rolls over the crossing at about 4 m/s and enters the junction.","masked":[]},{"name":"permit","expected":"compliant","narrative":"The same approach and the same crossing. Two seconds before the crossing the car's speed falls to zero and stays there for several observations, its body short of the crossing along the lane's designated direction and within the stop-point tolerance of it, its footprint overlapping neither the crossing nor the junction; it then moves off and enters the junction.","masked":[]},{"name":"idle","expected":"not_applicable","narrative":"A pedal cycle propelled by human power — a device the vehicle definition leaves out, so the aggregate is false for it — rides along the same stop-sign-governed lane and into the junction without halting anywhere. No vehicle is bound and the rule does not engage.","masked":[]},{"name":"blind","expected":"unknown","narrative":"The forbid approach, with the source declaring the speed of road users absent: the trigger is decided (the lane, its entrance into the junction, the stop sign's governance and the entry are all recorded), but no observation of the approach decides whether the car came to a complete cessation from movement, so the search for the act neither finds it nor excludes it.","masked":["kin.speed"]},{"name":"history_boundary","expected":"unknown","narrative":"The recording begins with the car already over the stop line and short of the junction, its body nearer the mark than the stop-point tolerance, so no observation at which it was outside the mark's stopping zone upstream is recorded; it enters the junction two observations later without halting in the recorded part. The search back from the entry reaches neither the start of the approach nor a previous entry of this car into this junction, and no recorded halt decides the duty.","boundary":"the approach the trace lacks: the observations between the car's exit from the stop line's stopping zone upstream and the start of the recording, in which the halt the duty requires could have been made"}],"literals":[],"param_proposals":[{"name":"p.standstill_speed_tolerance","unit":"m/s","value":0.1,"convention":"Standstill convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed reading is read as the definition's complete cessation from movement, set at the noise floor of vehicle speed measurement so that a standing vehicle is not reported as moving and a creeping one is not reported as halted.","source":"stop-detection thresholds used in naturalistic-driving and vehicle-dynamics data reduction"},{"name":"p.stop_point_tolerance","unit":"m","value":1.0,"convention":"Stop-point convention of the approach reading: the bound within which a halt counts as at the place the words name (the crossing, the stop line, the view point), covering the lateral and longitudinal error of the map's mark and of the body outline.","source":"stop-line compliance field studies and lane-level map accuracy specifications"},{"name":"p.intersecting_way_view_distance","unit":"m","value":100.0,"convention":"Intersection sight-distance convention: the length of the intersecting way that must be visible in each direction from the stopping point for a driver to judge a gap and clear the junction, taken from the departure sight triangle for a minor-road stop at a major road of ordinary speed.","source":"AASHTO Green Book, intersection sight distance (case B)"}],"gaps":[]}

{"node_id":"NRS_484B_113_2","law_refs":["NRS-484B-113-2"],"subject":{"binder":"v","class_elements":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"]},"segmentation":[{"id":"s1","text":"The driver of a vehicle:","role":"subject"},{"id":"s2","text":"Shall not back into an intersection, on or over a crosswalk, or around a","role":"obligation"},{"id":"s3","text":"street","role":"condition"},{"id":"s4","text":"corner.","role":"condition"}],"elements":[{"span":"s1","atoms":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"],"derived":[],"justification":"“vehicle” is the term DEF-NRS-484A-320 defines and the run admits as DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, so the span claims ru.aggregate with that id: “membership of a legal aggregate … true when the user carries an included class, unknown when no included class holds and the user carries an unresolved class”. The exclusion “not a stand-in for a named road-user class” is respected (the aggregate is claimed as the aggregate, never expanded into classes), and the exclusion of relational roles is respected by reading “driver” through controlled motion (narrowing on this span)."},{"span":"s2","atoms":["st.intersection","st.crosswalk","rel.occupies"],"derived":["drv.motion.reverse_travel"],"justification":"“back” is rearward motion: drv.motion.reverse_travel states that the component of the road user's velocity along its own heading is rearward beyond a tolerance, which is how the ontology directs the word to be read — kin.gear “is not a stand-in for the direction of motion — a vehicle in a forward gear rolls backwards on a grade; backing is read from kinematics”. “into an intersection” is the entry event into st.intersection, “the region where two roadways meet, bounded by the prolongation of their edges”, whose contract also carries the definition's third clause, since “a junction where an alley meets another way … is no intersection but a st.driveway_or_alley_entrance”, matching DEF-NRS-484A-105(3). “on or over a crosswalk” is st.crosswalk, “marked crossing, or the unmarked prolongation of sidewalks at an intersection; marked attribute”, which is DEF-NRS-484A-065's two limbs. rel.occupies, “a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region (… intersection, crosswalk …)”, is the anchor for both places: the entry is its rise for the junction, and being on or over the crossing is the overlap itself."},{"span":"s4","atoms":["st.intersection","st.highway","st.on_way","rel.occupies"],"derived":["drv.motion.turning"],"justification":"A corner is the corner of a junction of ways: st.intersection is “the region where two roadways meet”, st.highway “the entire width between the boundary lines of every way dedicated to a public authority when any part of the way is open to the use of the public for purposes of vehicular traffic” — DEF-NRS-484A-265's observable content for “street” — and st.on_way, “the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on … an intersection lies on every way that meets there”, is what makes the junction one of two ways rather than a bare region. rel.occupies anchors the corner to the subject: the vehicle's footprint overlaps that junction region. “around” is the bending of the path through the corner, carried by drv.motion.turning, whose heading change over the window behind the observation stands clear of the source's resolution; {"concept_id":"drv.motion.standstill","kind":"formula","contract":"The road user is motionless at the observation: the magnitude of its velocity is at most the speed tolerance, a speed the caller sets, so that a sampled reading at or below it is read as no movement at all. The definition this contract carries requires a “complete cessation from movement”, and because speed is sampled and measured with error, the tolerance is the bound within which a reading is read as that cessation; it is the contract's own magnitude and never a figure. The concept states the motion state at the observation and nothing else. The atom carries no exclusion bearing on this reading; kin.velocity is not read, because the definition speaks of movement and not of its direction."}],"residues":[{"span":"when required","why":"The definition's scope clause tells which of the two posted definitions of the word applies to a given law — the one for a stop that is required rather than prohibited. {"concept_id":"drv.interaction.vehicle_file","kind":"formula","contract":"Road user u is one of a file of road users travelling one behind another at the observation: counting u itself, at least the minimum member count of road users have their heading aligned with u's within the same-direction tolerance, lie ahead of or behind u in the same lane, and are within the file reach of u, a distance the caller sets measured between the nearest points of the bodies. {"concept_id":"drv.motion.left_turn","kind":"formula","contract":"The road user has turned to the left: counting from the onset of the turning — the observation at which its rate of change of heading to the left first rose above the onset yaw rate, a rate the caller sets — the heading change accumulated since that onset reaches at least the turn angle, a size the caller sets, to the left. lines: {"node_id":"NRS_484A_450_2","law_refs":["NRS-484A-450-2"],"subject":{"binder":"v","class_elements":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"]},"segmentation":[{"id":"s1","text":"Every driver of a vehicle","role":"subject"},{"id":"s2","text":"approaching a stop intersection indicated by a stop sign","role":"trigger"},{"id":"s3","text":"shall stop before entering the crosswalk on the near side of the intersection or, if there is no crosswalk, shall stop at a clearly marked stop line, or if none, then at the point nearest the intersecting highway","role":"obligation"},{"id":"s4","text":"where the driver has a view of approaching traffic on the intersecting highway","role":"standard"},{"id":"s5","text":"before entering the intersection.","role":"condition"}],"elements":[{"span":"s1","atoms":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"],"derived":[],"justification":"“vehicle” is the term DEF-NRS-484A-320 defines and the run admits as the aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, so the span claims ru.aggregate with that id: the atom is “membership of a legal aggregate: the atom's literal argument is an aggregate id”, true where the road user carries an included class, unknown where an included or unresolved class it might carry is unobserved. Its exclusion “not a stand-in for a named road-user class” does not apply, because the admitted aggregate is claimed as the aggregate and never replaced by a class atom; its exclusion of “a relational role such as who drives or controls a vehicle” is respected by reading “driver” through the vehicle's controlled motion (narrowing on this span) rather than as a member of the aggregate."},{"span":"s2","atoms":["st.intersection","st.travel_region","rel.occupies","st.lane_enters","dev.stop_sign","dev.governs"],"derived":[],"justification":"The approach is read as the ontology's section on an act due at a place before an event states it: “a road user's approach to an intersection is a carrier it occupies (rel.occupies) whose entrance end is that intersection”. st.intersection is “the region where two roadways meet, bounded by the prolongation of their edges”, the region the words call the intersection; st.travel_region is the kind the carrier quantifier ranges over, “the union of the kinds a device can govern … a lane and the kinds that refine it, a bicycle lane or path, a roadway and the kinds that refine it, a shoulder, or an intersection”, which is exactly the set of carriers st.lane_enters admits, so each region argument of the claimed relations has a claimed kind; st.lane_enters is “the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end”, and its clause “it is entry topology: it is decided where the source records it … never inferred from distance, overlap or a road user's velocity” is why approaching is not read from heading or closing speed. dev.stop_sign is the “regulatory sign requiring a full halt”, the sign the words name, and dev.governs, “the travel regions whose traffic the device controls … or an intersection”, ties it to the carrier the vehicle approaches through, as the ontology directs (“the mark that governs that approach is one the source records as marking that carrier”); dev.governs's exclusion “not a stand-in for a position” does not apply, because the place of the halt is read from the crosswalk, the stop line or the view point in s3 and never from where the sign stands. rel.occupies is “a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region”, the anchor that makes the carrier the subject's own."},{"span":"s3","atoms":["st.crosswalk","st.stop_line","st.travel_region","st.entrance_of","st.lane_direction","st.region_geometry","rel.occupies","st.intersection","st.highway","st.on_way","prim.region_offset_along"],"derived":["drv.motion.standstill"],"justification":"“shall stop” is the act: drv.motion.standstill carries the posted definition DEF-NRS-484A-255, “complete cessation from movement”, as a motion state at an observation, with the speed tolerance the sampling leaves to the observer. The first place is the crosswalk “on the near side of the intersection”: st.crosswalk is the “marked crossing, or the unmarked prolongation of sidewalks at an intersection”, and which crossing is the near one is st.entrance_of, “the carrier whose entrance into an intersection a stop line or a crosswalk marks — exactly that carrier's entrance, the line or crossing a vehicle approaching through that carrier halts at or before”, read on the same carrier st.lane_enters relates to the intersection; st.entrance_of's exclusion “not a stand-in for distance to the line” is why nearness never selects the crossing. The second place is st.stop_line, “the transverse line marking where vehicles halt for a device”, taken where the crosswalk's observed list of entrances excludes the carrier, as st.entrance_of's completeness clause permits. The third is the point nearest the intersecting highway, read on the carrier (st.travel_region) against the way the junction lies on: st.highway is “the entire width between the boundary lines of every way”, st.on_way “the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on — … an intersection lies on every way that meets there”, so the intersecting highway is a way the intersection lies on other than the one the carrier lies on.
