lines: {"node_id":"NRS_484A_450_2","law_refs":["NRS-484A-450-2"],"subject":{"binder":"v","class_elements":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"]},"segmentation":[{"id":"s1","text":"Every driver of a vehicle","role":"subject"},{"id":"s2","text":"approaching a stop intersection indicated by a stop sign","role":"trigger"},{"id":"s3","text":"shall stop before entering the crosswalk on the near side of the intersection or, if there is no crosswalk, shall stop at a clearly marked stop line, or if none, then at the point nearest the intersecting highway","role":"obligation"},{"id":"s4","text":"where the driver has a view of approaching traffic on the intersecting highway","role":"standard"},{"id":"s5","text":"before entering the intersection.","role":"condition"}],"elements":[{"span":"s1","atoms":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"],"derived":[],"justification":"“vehicle” is the term DEF-NRS-484A-320 defines and the run admits as the aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, so the span claims ru.aggregate with that id: the atom is “membership of a legal aggregate: the atom's literal argument is an aggregate id”, true where the road user carries an included class, unknown where an included or unresolved class it might carry is unobserved. Its exclusion “not a stand-in for a named road-user class” does not apply, because the admitted aggregate is claimed as the aggregate and never replaced by a class atom; its exclusion of “a relational role such as who drives or controls a vehicle” is respected by reading “driver” through the vehicle's controlled motion (narrowing on this span) rather than as a member of the aggregate."},{"span":"s2","atoms":["st.intersection","st.travel_region","rel.occupies","st.lane_enters","dev.stop_sign","dev.governs"],"derived":[],"justification":"The approach is read as the ontology's section on an act due at a place before an event states it: “a road user's approach to an intersection is a carrier it occupies (rel.occupies) whose entrance end is that intersection”. st.intersection is “the region where two roadways meet, bounded by the prolongation of their edges”, the region the words call the intersection; st.travel_region is the kind the carrier quantifier ranges over, “the union of the kinds a device can govern … a lane and the kinds that refine it, a bicycle lane or path, a roadway and the kinds that refine it, a shoulder, or an intersection”, which is exactly the set of carriers st.lane_enters admits, so each region argument of the claimed relations has a claimed kind; st.lane_enters is “the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end”, and its clause “it is entry topology: it is decided where the source records it … never inferred from distance, overlap or a road user's velocity” is why approaching is not read from heading or closing speed. dev.stop_sign is the “regulatory sign requiring a full halt”, the sign the words name, and dev.governs, “the travel regions whose traffic the device controls … or an intersection”, ties it to the carrier the vehicle approaches through, as the ontology directs (“the mark that governs that approach is one the source records as marking that carrier”); dev.governs's exclusion “not a stand-in for a position” does not apply, because the place of the halt is read from the crosswalk, the stop line or the view point in s3 and never from where the sign stands. rel.occupies is “a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region”, the anchor that makes the carrier the subject's own."},{"span":"s3","atoms":["st.crosswalk","st.stop_line","st.travel_region","st.entrance_of","st.lane_direction","st.region_geometry","rel.occupies","st.intersection","st.highway","st.on_way","prim.region_offset_along"],"derived":["drv.motion.standstill"],"justification":"“shall stop” is the act: drv.motion.standstill carries the posted definition DEF-NRS-484A-255, “complete cessation from movement”, as a motion state at an observation, with the speed tolerance the sampling leaves to the observer. The first place is the crosswalk “on the near side of the intersection”: st.crosswalk is the “marked crossing, or the unmarked prolongation of sidewalks at an intersection”, and which crossing is the near one is st.entrance_of, “the carrier whose entrance into an intersection a stop line or a crosswalk marks — exactly that carrier's entrance, the line or crossing a vehicle approaching through that carrier halts at or before”, read on the same carrier st.lane_enters relates to the intersection; st.entrance_of's exclusion “not a stand-in for distance to the line” is why nearness never selects the crossing. The second place is st.stop_line, “the transverse line marking where vehicles halt for a device”, taken where the crosswalk's observed list of entrances excludes the carrier, as st.entrance_of's completeness clause permits. The third is the point nearest the intersecting highway, read on the carrier (st.travel_region) against the way the junction lies on: st.highway is “the entire width between the boundary lines of every way”, st.on_way “the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on — … an intersection lies on every way that meets there”, so the intersecting highway is a way the intersection lies on other than the one the carrier lies on. That the halt is at the place and on the near side of it is st.region_geometry, “the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it”, within p.stop_point_tolerance, with the side taken from prim.region_offset_along, “the signed distance … measured along a carrier's designated direction (st.lane_direction)”, whose sign gives the side as the ontology requires (“the side of the mark is read along that carrier's designated direction … never along the road user's heading”); the primitive's own inputs are not claimed again beyond st.lane_direction and st.region_geometry, which the rule also reads on their own for the direction and for the distance, since prim.region_offset_along “is a geometric quantity only … a distance to the region is read from st.region_geometry, never from this value”. rel.occupies excludes a halt whose footprint already overlaps the crossing or the junction, which the words place the halt before, and st.intersection is the region that entry concerns."},{"span":"s5","atoms":["st.intersection","rel.occupies"],"derived":[],"justification":"“before entering the intersection” is the event the duty is owed before: the observation at which the vehicle's footprint first overlaps the intersection region. rel.occupies is “a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region (… intersection …)” and st.intersection the region itself; st.intersection's exclusion “not a stand-in for a crosswalk or a stop line — a stop before the crossing is earlier than a stop before the intersection” is precisely the distinction kept here, the crossing being the place of the act in s3 and the junction the event in this span."}],"operationalizations":[{"span":"s4","standard":"where the driver has a view of approaching traffic on the intersecting highway","concepts":["st.sight_along_way","st.highway","st.on_way","st.intersection","rel.visible","ru.aggregate","st.travel_region","rel.occupies"],"params":["p.intersecting_way_view_distance"],"convention":"Intersection sight-distance convention (AASHTO Green Book intersection sight distance, the departure-sight-triangle cases): a driver halted at the stopping point must be able to see along the major way at least the distance an approaching vehicle travels in the time needed to judge a gap and clear the junction. The point is adequate where st.sight_along_way, “the distance along a way, in each direction from the point of that way nearest a road user, within which another vehicle on that way could be seen from the road user's eye at the observation … the smaller of the two directions”, taken for the intersecting highway the junction lies on (st.highway with st.on_way and st.intersection), is at least p.intersecting_way_view_distance, and where a road user that is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic is on that way approaching the junction, that road user is visible from the vehicle (rel.visible, “b is visible from a: an unobstructed line of sight”). The aggregate fixes whose approach counts as the traffic to be seen — “pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances … using any highway for purposes of travel” — and the sight atom carries the view itself, since rel.visible “is not a stand-in for … the sight distance of a place” and st.sight_along_way is “not a stand-in for … whether an actual road user is seen”: the two together read the span's words where a road user is present and where none is. p.intersecting_way_view_distance is the only magnitude, and it is the reading's, not the words'.","surrogate":false}],"assumptions":[],"intentions":[],"compositions":[],"residues":[],"binders":[{"name":"v","class_elements":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"]}],"applicability":"The bound road user is a vehicle of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle that occupies a travel region whose entrance end is an intersection (st.lane_enters on that carrier) and that a stop sign governs (dev.stop_sign with dev.governs on that same carrier), and that enters that intersection: the stop intersection indicated by a stop sign which it approaches. Where the sign's governance of the carrier is unobserved, whether the rule applies is unknown; where the source's complete record shows the sign governs no carrier the vehicle occupies, the rule does not apply.","obligation":"At each observation at which the vehicle's footprint first overlaps the intersection it approaches (the entry event: the rise of rel.occupies of the vehicle on the intersection X that the carrier it occupies runs into, st.lane_enters, read from this observation and the one before it), the vehicle must have been at a standstill (drv.motion.standstill with p.standstill_speed_tolerance) at some observation of the approach that leads to that entry, with its body at the place the words name. The place is read from the words in their order: first the crosswalk that marks the entrance of the carrier the vehicle approaches through (st.entrance_of on the same carrier st.lane_enters relates to X); where that crosswalk's entrances are observed, so that its list is complete, and exclude the carrier, the clearly marked stop line that marks it; where neither marks it, the point on the carrier nearest the intersecting highway at which the view of s4 is met. Where a mark's association with the carrier is not observed, whether that mark governs is unknown and the duty is unknown on that ground. A halt counts at the place where the distance from the vehicle's body to the mark (st.region_geometry) is within p.stop_point_tolerance and the mark lies ahead along the carrier's designated direction (the sign of prim.region_offset_along with st.lane_direction); the words placing the halt before the vehicle enters the crossing and the junction, a halt at which its footprint already overlaps that region (rel.occupies) is not at the place, and the tolerance applies outside that region only. The search for the halt runs back from the entry event and ends only at the start of that approach — the last observation before the event at which the vehicle, on a carrier the mark marks, is off the mark, short of it and farther from it than p.stop_point_tolerance — or at the previous entry of the same vehicle into the same intersection; nothing else ends it: not another junction or mark, not the start of the recording, not a first observation, not a distance travelled. Only an observed exit from the stopping zone upstream begins a new approach, so a vehicle that leaves the zone upstream and returns owes the halt again, while crossing the mark, moving on toward the junction, a change of carrier, a lateral move or a reverse within the zone begin none and lose no halt already made. Where the search finds the halt the duty is met; where it reaches either end without the halt the duty is violated; where it reaches neither end without finding it — the recording begins inside the stopping zone, the observation before the event does not show the vehicle's place relative to the mark through its carrier, or the speed that decides the standstill is unobserved — the duty is unknown. Each entry owes its own halt: a halt made before the previous entry of the same vehicle into the same intersection discharged that entry, not this one.","params":["p.standstill_speed_tolerance","p.stop_point_tolerance","p.intersecting_way_view_distance"],"narrowings":[{"span":"s1","why":"“Every driver of a vehicle” is read as the vehicle whose motion is controlled. Who or what controls a road user is not observable, and the ontology reads “drives”, “operates” and “the driver” through the vehicle's controlled motion, a vehicle moving on the road being taken to be driven, with the duty binding that vehicle's conduct whoever or whatever is at the controls.","kind":"observable_reading","category":"agency"},{"span":"s2","why":"“indicated by a stop sign” is read as the presence of a stop sign governing the approach. That a sign is official or posted by an authority is a legal status the ontology reads through the feature itself: the sign's presence on the road is the evidence of the designation the section's title speaks of.","kind":"observable_reading","category":"status"},{"span":"s3","why":"“a clearly marked stop line” is read as the stop line the scene represents. The ontology states this reading for exactly these words: the line's presence is the evidence, and the paint's clarity or wear is not modelled. The reading relaxes nothing about which place governs, the act or its timing.","kind":"observable_reading","category":"status"},{"span":"s3","why":"“the point nearest the intersecting highway where the driver has a view” is read as a point on the carrier the vehicle approaches through, rather than any point of the scene: the words single out the vehicle's own approach, and the place is read on the region the node binds. Among the points of that carrier at which the view of s4 is met, the duty is read as met by a halt at or before the nearest such point to the intersecting highway, within p.stop_point_tolerance of it, so a halt farther back on the same carrier that still meets the view is not a violation; this is the reading of “the point nearest … where the driver has a view”, which names a nearest point among those with a view and not a single surveyed spot.","kind":"reading"},{"span":"s4","why":"“the driver has a view of approaching traffic” is read as what could be seen along the intersecting way from where the vehicle stands, and as the visibility of a road user of the traffic aggregate that is there. What a driver perceived is not observable; the ontology directs that where the words offer observable evidence the rule reads it, “what was in an actual road user's line of sight is rel.visible; what could be seen from or at a place is st.sight_distance”, and st.sight_along_way is that quantity measured along the way for a road user at the observation.","kind":"observable_reading","category":"perception"}],"scenarios":[{"name":"forbid","expected":"violated","narrative":"A car runs along a marked lane that the source records as entering a four-way junction, and a stop sign governs that lane. From the last observation at which the car is off the crossing, short of it and more than the stop-point tolerance from it, through to the observation at which its footprint first overlaps the junction, its speed never falls to the standstill tolerance: it rolls over the crossing at about 4 m/s and enters the junction.","masked":[]},{"name":"permit","expected":"compliant","narrative":"The same approach and the same crossing. The search back from the entry reaches neither the start of the approach nor a previous entry of this car into this junction, and no recorded halt decides the duty.","boundary":"the approach the trace lacks: the observations between the car's exit from the stop line's stopping zone upstream and the start of the recording, in which the halt the duty requires could have been made"}],"literals":[],"param_proposals":[{"name":"p.standstill_speed_tolerance","unit":"m/s","value":0.1,"convention":"Standstill convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed reading is read as the definition's complete cessation from movement, set at the noise floor of vehicle speed measurement so that a standing vehicle is not reported as moving and a creeping one is not reported as halted.","source":"stop-detection thresholds used in naturalistic-driving and vehicle-dynamics data reduction"},{"name":"p.stop_point_tolerance","unit":"m","value":1.0,"convention":"Stop-point convention of the approach reading: the bound within which a halt counts as at the place the words name (the crossing, the stop line, the view point), covering the lateral and longitudinal error of the map's mark and of the body outline.","source":"stop-line compliance field studies and lane-level map accuracy specifications"},{"name":"p.intersecting_way_view_distance","unit":"m","value":100.0,"convention":"Intersection sight-distance convention: the length of the intersecting way that must be visible in each direction from the stopping point for a driver to judge a gap and clear the junction, taken from the departure sight triangle for a minor-road stop at a major road of ordinary speed.","source":"AASHTO Green Book, intersection sight distance (case B)"}],"gaps":[]}

backing is read from kinematics”. “into an intersection” is the entry event into st.intersection, “the region where two roadways meet, bounded by the prolongation of their edges”, whose contract also carries the definition's third clause, since “a junction where an alley meets another way … is no intersection but a st.driveway_or_alley_entrance”, matching DEF-NRS-484A-105(3). “on or over a crosswalk” is st.crosswalk, “marked crossing, or the unmarked prolongation of sidewalks at an intersection; marked attribute”, which is DEF-NRS-484A-065's two limbs. rel.occupies, “a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region (… intersection, crosswalk …)”, is the anchor for both places: the entry is its rise for the junction, and being on or over the crossing is the overlap itself."},{"span":"s4","atoms":["st.intersection","st.highway","st.on_way","rel.occupies"],"derived":["drv.motion.turning"],"justification":"A corner is the corner of a junction of ways: st.intersection is “the region where two roadways meet”, st.highway “the entire width between the boundary lines of every way dedicated to a public authority when any part of the way is open to the use of the public for purposes of vehicular traffic” — DEF-NRS-484A-265's observable content for “street” — and st.on_way, “the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on … an intersection lies on every way that meets there”, is what makes the junction one of two ways rather than a bare region. rel.occupies anchors the corner to the subject: the vehicle's footprint overlaps that junction region. “around” is the bending of the path through the corner, carried by drv.motion.turning, whose heading change over the window behind the observation stands clear of the source's resolution; lines: {"node_id":"NRS_484A_450_2","law_refs":["NRS-484A-450-2"],"subject":{"binder":"v","class_elements":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"]},"segmentation":[{"id":"s1","text":"Every driver of a vehicle","role":"subject"},{"id":"s2","text":"approaching a stop intersection indicated by a stop sign","role":"trigger"},{"id":"s3","text":"shall stop before entering the crosswalk on the near side of the intersection or, if there is no crosswalk, shall stop at a clearly marked stop line, or if none, then at the point nearest the intersecting highway","role":"obligation"},{"id":"s4","text":"where the driver has a view of approaching traffic on the intersecting highway","role":"standard"},{"id":"s5","text":"before entering the intersection.","role":"condition"}],"elements":[{"span":"s1","atoms":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"],"derived":[],"justification":"“vehicle” is the term DEF-NRS-484A-320 defines and the run admits as the aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, so the span claims ru.aggregate with that id: the atom is “membership of a legal aggregate: the atom's literal argument is an aggregate id”, true where the road user carries an included class, unknown where an included or unresolved class it might carry is unobserved. Its exclusion “not a stand-in for a named road-user class” does not apply, because the admitted aggregate is claimed as the aggregate and never replaced by a class atom; its exclusion of “a relational role such as who drives or controls a vehicle” is respected by reading “driver” through the vehicle's controlled motion (narrowing on this span) rather than as a member of the aggregate."},{"span":"s2","atoms":["st.intersection","st.travel_region","rel.occupies","st.lane_enters","dev.stop_sign","dev.governs"],"derived":[],"justification":"The approach is read as the ontology's section on an act due at a place before an event states it: “a road user's approach to an intersection is a carrier it occupies (rel.occupies) whose entrance end is that intersection”. st.intersection is “the region where two roadways meet, bounded by the prolongation of their edges”, the region the words call the intersection; st.travel_region is the kind the carrier quantifier ranges over, “the union of the kinds a device can govern … a lane and the kinds that refine it, a bicycle lane or path, a roadway and the kinds that refine it, a shoulder, or an intersection”, which is exactly the set of carriers st.lane_enters admits, so each region argument of the claimed relations has a claimed kind; st.lane_enters is “the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end”, and its clause “it is entry topology: it is decided where the source records it … never inferred from distance, overlap or a road user's velocity” is why approaching is not read from heading or closing speed. dev.stop_sign is the “regulatory sign requiring a full halt”, the sign the words name, and dev.governs, “the travel regions whose traffic the device controls … or an intersection”, ties it to the carrier the vehicle approaches through, as the ontology directs (“the mark that governs that approach is one the source records as marking that carrier”); dev.governs's exclusion “not a stand-in for a position” does not apply, because the place of the halt is read from the crosswalk, the stop line or the view point in s3 and never from where the sign stands. rel.occupies is “a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region”, the anchor that makes the carrier the subject's own."},{"span":"s3","atoms":["st.crosswalk","st.stop_line","st.travel_region","st.entrance_of","st.lane_direction","st.region_geometry","rel.occupies","st.intersection","st.highway","st.on_way","prim.region_offset_along"],"derived":["drv.motion.standstill"],"justification":"“shall stop” is the act: drv.motion.standstill carries the posted definition DEF-NRS-484A-255, “complete cessation from movement”, as a motion state at an observation, with the speed tolerance the sampling leaves to the observer. The first place is the crosswalk “on the near side of the intersection”: st.crosswalk is the “marked crossing, or the unmarked prolongation of sidewalks at an intersection”, and which crossing is the near one is st.entrance_of, “the carrier whose entrance into an intersection a stop line or a crosswalk marks — exactly that carrier's entrance, the line or crossing a vehicle approaching through that carrier halts at or before”, read on the same carrier st.lane_enters relates to the intersection; st.entrance_of's exclusion “not a stand-in for distance to the line” is why nearness never selects the crossing. The second place is st.stop_line, “the transverse line marking where vehicles halt for a device”, taken where the crosswalk's observed list of entrances excludes the carrier, as st.entrance_of's completeness clause permits. The third is the point nearest the intersecting highway, read on the carrier (st.travel_region) against the way the junction lies on: st.highway is “the entire width between the boundary lines of every way”, st.on_way “the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on — … an intersection lies on every way that meets there”, so the intersecting highway is a way the intersection lies on other than the one the carrier lies on. That the halt is at the place and on the near side of it is st.region_geometry, “the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it”, within p.stop_point_tolerance, with the side taken from prim.region_offset_along, “the signed distance … measured along a carrier's designated direction (st.lane_direction)”, whose sign gives the side as the ontology requires (“the side of the mark is read along that carrier's designated direction … never along the road user's heading”); lines: {"concept_id":"drv.motion.standstill","kind":"formula","contract":"The road user is motionless at the observation: the magnitude of its velocity is at most the speed tolerance, a speed the caller sets, so that a sampled reading at or below it is read as no movement at all. The definition this contract carries requires a “complete cessation from movement”, and because speed is sampled and measured with error, the tolerance is the bound within which a reading is read as that cessation; it is the contract's own magnitude and never a figure. The concept states the motion state at the observation and nothing else. Not a stand-in for: a halt of any duration or a halt repeated over a window, a vehicle standing, parked or waiting, the engine being off or a brake being applied, or a halt at a place a law names — it carries no place, no duration and no control state.","definition":"DEF-NRS-484A-255","args":[{"name":"u","sort":"track"}],"params":[{"name":"speed_tolerance","unit":"m/s","meaning":"the speed at or below which a sampled reading of the road user's speed is read as a complete cessation from movement; it names the source's resolution for a standing body"}],"elements":[{"span":"the magnitude of its velocity is at most the speed tolerance","atoms":["kin.speed"],"concepts":[],"justification":"kin.speed is the “magnitude of velocity” of a road user, in m/s, which is exactly the quantity the definition's “complete cessation from movement” bounds. The atom carries no exclusion bearing on this reading; kin.velocity is not read, because the definition speaks of movement and not of its direction."}],"residues":[{"span":"when required","why":"The definition's scope clause tells which of the two posted definitions of the word applies to a given law — the one for a stop that is required rather than prohibited. {"concept_id":"drv.motion.reverse_travel","kind":"formula","contract":"The road user is travelling rearward at the observation: the component of its velocity along the direction its body points is at most the negative of the reverse speed tolerance, a speed the caller sets, so that a rearward component smaller than it is read as none. {"concept_id":"drv.motion.turning","kind":"formula","contract":"The road user's heading is changing at the observation: the magnitude of its heading change over the window behind the observation is at least the heading change tolerance, a size the caller sets at the resolution of the source. {"concept_id":"drv.interaction.vehicle_file","kind":"formula","contract":"Road user u is one of a file of road users travelling one behind another at the observation: counting u itself, at least the minimum member count of road users have their heading aligned with u's within the same-direction tolerance, lie ahead of or behind u in the same lane, and are within the file reach of u, a distance the caller sets measured between the nearest points of the bodies. {"concept_id":"drv.lane.lane_change","kind":"formula","contract":"The road user crosses out of a structure region at the observation: its footprint overlapped the region at the observation before, and at the observation it either no longer overlaps that region or overlaps a lane neighbouring it in the same direction of travel which it did not overlap at the observation before. lines: {"concept_id":"drv.motion.turning","kind":"formula","contract":"The road user's heading is changing at the observation: the magnitude of its heading change over the window behind the observation is at least the heading change tolerance, a size the caller sets at the resolution of the source. {"concept_id":"drv.interaction.overtaking","kind":"formula","contract":"Road user a is passing road user b at the observation: the two headings are aligned within the same-direction tolerance, a's speed exceeds b's by at least the speed excess the caller sets, and either the two bodies' projections on a's heading overlap — a is drawing level with b — or b is still ahead of a in the same lane. lines: {"concept_id":"drv.interaction.vehicle_file","kind":"formula","contract":"Road user u is one of a file of road users travelling one behind another at the observation: counting u itself, at least the minimum member count of road users have their heading aligned with u's within the same-direction tolerance, lie ahead of or behind u in the same lane, and are within the file reach of u, a distance the caller sets measured between the nearest points of the bodies. It is a relation of place, direction and spacing at the observation. It says nothing of why the road users travel together, of a common destination or origin, of an organizer, or of their speed: a caller that means a moving file states the motion itself. Not a stand-in for: a chain each of whose consecutive spaces is bounded — the reach is measured from u to each member, so a long file is read through the membership of each road user in turn — the class of the members, which the caller states, or a towed combination, which is one road user drawn by another.","definition":null,"args":[{"name":"u","sort":"track"}],"params":[{"name":"min_member_count","unit":"count","meaning":"the number of road users, u included, at which the group is read as a file rather than as road users happening to follow one another"},{"name":"file_reach","unit":"m","meaning":"the distance between the nearest points of two bodies within which another road user is read as travelling with u in the same file"},{"name":"same_direction_tolerance","unit":"ratio","meaning":"the cosine of the largest angle between two headings still read as the same direction, a ratio between minus one and one"}],"elements":[{"span":"have their heading aligned with u's within the same-direction tolerance","atoms":["rel.same_direction"],"concepts":[],"justification":"rel.same_direction is “headings aligned: the cosine of the angle between the headings is above its tolerance”, the relation this clause states, the tolerance being the atom's own parameter."},{"span":"lie ahead of or behind u in the same lane","atoms":["rel.ahead_behind_in_lane"],"concepts":[],"justification":"rel.ahead_behind_in_lane is “a is ahead of / behind b in the same lane, along the lane direction”, which is the one-behind-another arrangement this clause states; rel.bearing is not read, giving only a direction and not an in-lane order."},{"span":"are within the file reach of u, a distance … measured between the nearest points of the bodies","atoms":["rel.surface_gap"],"concepts":[],"justification":"rel.surface_gap is the “distance between the nearest points of two bodies, each body's footprint read with its own heading and extent”, which is the spacing this clause bounds; rel.centre_distance is excluded by its own contract as “not a stand-in for a clearance between bodies”."}],"residues":[],"literals":[],"scenarios":[{"name":"holds","expected":"compliant","narrative":"Five cars run in file in one lane of a rural highway, each within 20 m of the next and all headings aligned: each of them, counting itself, has at least three members of the group within the reach, ahead of or behind it in the lane.","masked":[]},{"name":"fails","expected":"violated","narrative":"One car runs alone in that lane with the nearest other road user 400 m ahead: the minimum member count is not reached within the reach.","masked":[]},{"name":"blind","expected":"unknown","narrative":"The five cars with the source declaring the gap between bodies absent: how far apart the members are, and so how many lie within the reach, cannot be read.","masked":["rel.surface_gap"]}],"used_by":["NRS_484B_127_3"],"supersedes":null}

{"concept_id":"drv.position.direction_component","kind":"quantity","contract":"The component, in metres per second, of a road user's velocity along the designated direction of travel of a structure region: positive where the road user moves with that direction, negative where it moves against it, and near zero where it stands or moves across it. The quantity is geometric only: it does not state that the road user is on the region, that the region is the one a law names, or how far the road user is from it, and a caller states those with its own relations. Unknown where the road user's velocity is absent and where the region carries no designated direction — a centre turn lane carries none, and a place no carrier covers has none. lines: {"concept_id":"drv.position.direction_component","kind":"quantity","contract":"The component, in metres per second, of a road user's velocity along the designated direction of travel of a structure region: positive where the road user moves with that direction, negative where it moves against it, and near zero where it stands or moves across it. The quantity is geometric only: it does not state that the road user is on the region, that the region is the one a law names, or how far the road user is from it, and a caller states those with its own relations. Unknown where the road user's velocity is absent and where the region carries no designated direction — a centre turn lane carries none, and a place no carrier covers has none. {"concept_id":"drv.interaction.vehicle_file","kind":"formula","contract":"Road user u is one of a file of road users travelling one behind another at the observation: counting u itself, at least the minimum member count of road users have their heading aligned with u's within the same-direction tolerance, lie ahead of or behind u in the same lane, and are within the file reach of u, a distance the caller sets measured between the nearest points of the bodies. Not a stand-in for: a chain each of whose consecutive spaces is bounded — the reach is measured from u to each member, so a long file is read through the membership of each road user in turn — the class of the members, which the caller states, or a towed combination, which is one road user drawn by another.","definition":null,"args":[{"name":"u","sort":"track"}],"params":[{"name":"min_member_count","unit":"count","meaning":"the number of road users, u included, at which the group is read as a file rather than as road users happening to follow one another"},{"name":"file_reach","unit":"m","meaning":"the distance between the nearest points of two bodies within which another road user is read as travelling with u in the same file"},{"name":"same_direction_tolerance","unit":"ratio","meaning":"the cosine of the largest angle between two headings still read as the same direction, a ratio between minus one and one"}],"elements":[{"span":"have their heading aligned with u's within the same-direction tolerance","atoms":["rel.same_direction"],"concepts":[],"justification":"rel.same_direction is “headings aligned: the cosine of the angle between the headings is above its tolerance”, the relation this clause states, the tolerance being the atom's own parameter."},{"span":"lie ahead of or behind u in the same lane","atoms":["rel.ahead_behind_in_lane"],"concepts":[],"justification":"rel.ahead_behind_in_lane is “a is ahead of / behind b in the same lane, along the lane direction”, which is the one-behind-another arrangement this clause states; {"concept_id":"drv.position.direction_component","kind":"quantity","contract":"The component, in metres per second, of a road user's velocity along the designated direction of travel of a structure region: positive where the road user moves with that direction, negative where it moves against it, and near zero where it stands or moves across it. Unknown where the road user's velocity is absent and where the region carries no designated direction — a centre turn lane carries none, and a place no carrier covers has none. Not a stand-in for: the direction the body points, which a road user may hold while moving another way, the road user's speed, which is unsigned, or an angle between the two directions.","definition":null,"args":[{"name":"u","sort":"track"},{"name":"r","sort":"region"}],"params":[],"elements":[{"span":"a road user's velocity","atoms":["kin.velocity"],"concepts":[],"justification":"kin.velocity is the “velocity vector” of a road user, in m/s in the world frame, whose components are what this quantity projects; {"concept_id":"drv.lane.lane_change","kind":"formula","contract":"The road user crosses out of a structure region at the observation: its footprint overlapped the region at the observation before, and at the observation it either no longer overlaps that region or overlaps a lane neighbouring it in the same direction of travel which it did not overlap at the observation before. {"concept_id":"drv.motion.left_turn","kind":"formula","contract":"The road user has turned to the left: counting from the onset of the turning — the observation at which its rate of change of heading to the left first rose above the onset yaw rate, a rate the caller sets — the heading change accumulated since that onset reaches at least the turn angle, a size the caller sets, to the left. The concept becomes true at the observation at which that angle is first reached, and it holds at the later observations at which the accumulated change still holds that angle, until a later onset starts the count again; the integration is bounded by the heading step, the largest interval between consecutive observations it may integrate across. Where no such onset is observed, with the rate of change of heading known at every observation from the one before it onwards and no interval between consecutive observations longer than the heading step, the concept is unknown and never false, so a turn begun before the recording is never read as one made within it. It states the turning of the body only: no place, no lane, no way and no destination. {"concept_id":"drv.motion.u_turn","kind":"formula","contract":"The road user's direction of travel upon a way has reversed: counting from the onset of the manoeuvre — the observation at which the magnitude of its rate of change of heading first rose above the onset yaw rate, a rate the caller sets — the magnitude of the heading change accumulated since that onset reaches at least the reversal angle, a size the caller sets below a half turn, while the road user's footprint overlaps a way. Where no such onset is observed, with the rate of change of heading known at every observation from the one before it onwards and no interval between consecutive observations longer than the heading step, the concept is unknown and never false, so a reversal begun before the recording is never read as one made within it. lines: -{"node_id":"NRS_484A_450_2","law_refs":["NRS-484A-450-2"],"subject":{"binder":"v","class_elements":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"]},"segmentation":[{"id":"s1","text":"Every driver of a vehicle","role":"subject"},{"id":"s2","text":"approaching a stop intersection indicated by a stop sign","role":"trigger"},{"id":"s3","text":"shall stop before entering the crosswalk on the near side of the intersection or, if there is no crosswalk, shall stop at a clearly marked stop line, or if none, then at the point nearest the intersecting highway","role":"obligation"},{"id":"s4","text":"where the driver has a view of approaching traffic on the intersecting highway","role":"standard"},{"id":"s5","text":"before entering the intersection.","role":"condition"}],"elements":[{"span":"s1","atoms":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"],"derived":[],"justification":"“vehicle” is the term DEF-NRS-484A-320 defines and the run admits as the aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, so the span claims ru.aggregate with that id: the atom is “membership of a legal aggregate: the atom's literal argument is an aggregate id”, true where the road user carries an included class, unknown where an included or unresolved class it might carry is unobserved. Its exclusion “not a stand-in for a named road-user class” does not apply, because the admitted aggregate is claimed as the aggregate and never replaced by a class atom; its exclusion of “a relational role such as who drives or controls a vehicle” is respected by reading “driver” through the vehicle's controlled motion (narrowing on this span) rather than as a member of the aggregate."},{"span":"s2","atoms":["st.intersection","st.travel_region","rel.occupies","st.lane_enters","dev.stop_sign","dev.governs"],"derived":[],"justification":"The approach is read as the ontology's section on an act due at a place before an event states it: “a road user's approach to an intersection is a carrier it occupies (rel.occupies) whose entrance end is that intersection”. st.intersection is “the region where two roadways meet, bounded by the prolongation of their edges”, the region the words call the intersection; st.travel_region is the kind the carrier quantifier ranges over, “the union of the kinds a device can govern … a lane and the kinds that refine it, a bicycle lane or path, a roadway and the kinds that refine it, a shoulder, or an intersection”, which is exactly the set of carriers st.lane_enters admits, so each region argument of the claimed relations has a claimed kind; st.lane_enters is “the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end”, and its clause “it is entry topology: it is decided where the source records it … never inferred from distance, overlap or a road user's velocity” is why approaching is not read from heading or closing speed. dev.stop_sign is the “regulatory sign requiring a full halt”, the sign the words name, and dev.governs, “the travel regions whose traffic the device controls … or an intersection”, ties it to the carrier the vehicle approaches through, as the ontology directs (“the mark that governs that approach is one the source records as marking that carrier”); dev.governs's exclusion “not a stand-in for a position” does not apply, because the place of the halt is read from the crosswalk, the stop line or the view point in s3 and never from where the sign stands. rel.occupies is “a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region”, the anchor that makes the carrier the subject's own."},{"span":"s3","atoms":["st.crosswalk","st.stop_line","st.travel_region","st.entrance_of","st.lane_direction","st.region_geometry","rel.occupies","st.intersection","st.highway","st.on_way","prim.region_offset_along"],"derived":["drv.motion.standstill"],"justification":"“shall stop” is the act: drv.motion.standstill carries the posted definition DEF-NRS-484A-255, “complete cessation from movement”, as a motion state at an observation, with the speed tolerance the sampling leaves to the observer. The first place is the crosswalk “on the near side of the intersection”: st.crosswalk is the “marked crossing, or the unmarked prolongation of sidewalks at an intersection”, and which crossing is the near one is st.entrance_of, “the carrier whose entrance into an intersection a stop line or a crosswalk marks — exactly that carrier's entrance, the line or crossing a vehicle approaching through that carrier halts at or before”, read on the same carrier st.lane_enters relates to the intersection; st.entrance_of's exclusion “not a stand-in for distance to the line” is why nearness never selects the crossing. The second place is st.stop_line, “the transverse line marking where vehicles halt for a device”, taken where the crosswalk's observed list of entrances excludes the carrier, as st.entrance_of's completeness clause permits. The third is the point nearest the intersecting highway, read on the carrier (st.travel_region) against the way the junction lies on: st.highway is “the entire width between the boundary lines of every way”, st.on_way “the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on — … an intersection lies on every way that meets there”, so the intersecting highway is a way the intersection lies on other than the one the carrier lies on. That the halt is at the place and on the near side of it is st.region_geometry, “the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it”, within p.stop_point_tolerance, with the side taken from prim.region_offset_along, “the signed distance … measured along a carrier's designated direction (st.lane_direction)”, whose sign gives the side as the ontology requires (“the side of the mark is read along that carrier's designated direction … never along the road user's heading”); the primitive's own inputs are not claimed again beyond st.lane_direction and st.region_geometry, which the rule also reads on their own for the direction and for the distance, since prim.region_offset_along “is a geometric quantity only … a distance to the region is read from st.region_geometry, never from this value”. rel.occupies excludes a halt whose footprint already overlaps the crossing or the junction, which the words place the halt before, and st.intersection is the region that entry concerns."},{"span":"s5","atoms":["st.intersection","rel.occupies"],"derived":[],"justification":"“before entering the intersection” is the event the duty is owed before: the observation at which the vehicle's footprint first overlaps the intersection region. rel.occupies is “a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region (… intersection …)” and st.intersection the region itself; st.intersection's exclusion “not a stand-in for a crosswalk or a stop line — a stop before the crossing is earlier than a stop before the intersection” is precisely the distinction kept here, the crossing being the place of the act in s3 and the junction the event in this span."}],"operationalizations":[{"span":"s4","standard":"where the driver has a view of approaching traffic on the intersecting highway","concepts":["st.sight_along_way","st.highway","st.on_way","st.intersection","rel.visible","ru.aggregate","st.travel_region","rel.occupies"],"params":["p.intersecting_way_view_distance"],"convention":"Intersection sight-distance convention (AASHTO Green Book intersection sight distance, the departure-sight-triangle cases): a driver halted at the stopping point must be able to see along the major way at least the distance an approaching vehicle travels in the time needed to judge a gap and clear the junction. The point is adequate where st.sight_along_way, “the distance along a way, in each direction from the point of that way nearest a road user, within which another vehicle on that way could be seen from the road user's eye at the observation … the smaller of the two directions”, taken for the intersecting highway the junction lies on (st.highway with st.on_way and st.intersection), is at least p.intersecting_way_view_distance, and where a road user that is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic is on that way approaching the junction, that road user is visible from the vehicle (rel.visible, “b is visible from a: an unobstructed line of sight”). Where the sign's governance of the carrier is unobserved, whether the rule applies is unknown; where the source's complete record shows the sign governs no carrier the vehicle occupies, the rule does not apply.","obligation":"At each observation at which the vehicle's footprint first overlaps the intersection it approaches (the entry event: the rise of rel.occupies of the vehicle on the intersection X that the carrier it occupies runs into, st.lane_enters, read from this observation and the one before it), the vehicle must have been at a standstill (drv.motion.standstill with p.standstill_speed_tolerance) at some observation of the approach that leads to that entry, with its body at the place the words name. The place is read from the words in their order: first the crosswalk that marks the entrance of the carrier the vehicle approaches through (st.entrance_of on the same carrier st.lane_enters relates to X); where that crosswalk's entrances are observed, so that its list is complete, and exclude the carrier, the clearly marked stop line that marks it; where neither marks it, the point on the carrier nearest the intersecting highway at which the view of s4 is met. Where a mark's association with the carrier is not observed, whether that mark governs is unknown and the duty is unknown on that ground. A halt counts at the place where the distance from the vehicle's body to the mark (st.region_geometry) is within p.stop_point_tolerance and the mark lies ahead along the carrier's designated direction (the sign of prim.region_offset_along with st.lane_direction); the words placing the halt before the vehicle enters the crossing and the junction, a halt at which its footprint already overlaps that region (rel.occupies) is not at the place, and the tolerance applies outside that region only. The search for the halt runs back from the entry event and ends only at the start of that approach — the last observation before the event at which the vehicle, on a carrier the mark marks, is off the mark, short of it and farther from it than p.stop_point_tolerance — or at the previous entry of the same vehicle into the same intersection; nothing else ends it: not another junction or mark, not the start of the recording, not a first observation, not a distance travelled. {"concept_id":"drv.interaction.vehicle_file","kind":"formula","contract":"Road user u is one of a file of road users travelling one behind another at the observation: counting u itself, at least the minimum member count of road users have their heading aligned with u's within the same-direction tolerance, lie ahead of or behind u in the same lane, and are within the file reach of u, a distance the caller sets measured between the nearest points of the bodies. {"concept_id":"drv.position.direction_component","kind":"quantity","contract":"The component, in metres per second, of a road user's velocity along the designated direction of travel of a structure region: positive where the road user moves with that direction, negative where it moves against it, and near zero where it stands or moves across it. Unknown where the road user's velocity is absent and where the region carries no designated direction — a centre turn lane carries none, and a place no carrier covers has none. {"concept_id":"drv.lane.lane_change","kind":"formula","contract":"The road user crosses out of a structure region at the observation: its footprint overlapped the region at the observation before, and at the observation it either no longer overlaps that region or overlaps a lane neighbouring it in the same direction of travel which it did not overlap at the observation before. {"concept_id":"drv.motion.left_turn","kind":"formula","contract":"The road user has turned to the left: counting from the onset of the turning — the observation at which its rate of change of heading to the left first rose above the onset yaw rate, a rate the caller sets — the heading change accumulated since that onset reaches at least the turn angle, a size the caller sets, to the left. Where no such onset is observed, with the rate of change of heading known at every observation from the one before it onwards and no interval between consecutive observations longer than the heading step, the concept is unknown and never false, so a turn begun before the recording is never read as one made within it. It states the turning of the body only: no place, no lane, no way and no destination. {"concept_id":"drv.motion.u_turn","kind":"formula","contract":"The road user's direction of travel upon a way has reversed: counting from the onset of the manoeuvre — the observation at which the magnitude of its rate of change of heading first rose above the onset yaw rate, a rate the caller sets — the magnitude of the heading change accumulated since that onset reaches at least the reversal angle, a size the caller sets below a half turn, while the road user's footprint overlaps a way. Where no such onset is observed, with the rate of change of heading known at every observation from the one before it onwards and no interval between consecutive observations longer than the heading step, the concept is unknown and never false, so a reversal begun before the recording is never read as one made within it. lines: -{"node_id":"NRS_484A_450_2","law_refs":["NRS-484A-450-2"],"subject":{"binder":"v","class_elements":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"]},"segmentation":[{"id":"s1","text":"Every driver of a vehicle","role":"subject"},{"id":"s2","text":"approaching a stop intersection indicated by a stop sign","role":"trigger"},{"id":"s3","text":"shall stop before entering the crosswalk on the near side of the intersection or, if there is no crosswalk, shall stop at a clearly marked stop line, or if none, then at the point nearest the intersecting highway","role":"obligation"},{"id":"s4","text":"where the driver has a view of approaching traffic on the intersecting highway","role":"standard"},{"id":"s5","text":"before entering the intersection.","role":"condition"}],"elements":[{"span":"s1","atoms":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"],"derived":[],"justification":"“vehicle” is the term DEF-NRS-484A-320 defines and the run admits as the aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, so the span claims ru.aggregate with that id: the atom is “membership of a legal aggregate: the atom's literal argument is an aggregate id”, true where the road user carries an included class, unknown where an included or unresolved class it might carry is unobserved. Its exclusion “not a stand-in for a named road-user class” does not apply, because the admitted aggregate is claimed as the aggregate and never replaced by a class atom; its exclusion of “a relational role such as who drives or controls a vehicle” is respected by reading “driver” through the vehicle's controlled motion (narrowing on this span) rather than as a member of the aggregate."},{"span":"s2","atoms":["st.intersection","st.travel_region","rel.occupies","st.lane_enters","dev.stop_sign","dev.governs"],"derived":[],"justification":"The approach is read as the ontology's section on an act due at a place before an event states it: “a road user's approach to an intersection is a carrier it occupies (rel.occupies) whose entrance end is that intersection”. st.intersection is “the region where two roadways meet, bounded by the prolongation of their edges”, the region the words call the intersection; st.travel_region is the kind the carrier quantifier ranges over, “the union of the kinds a device can govern … a lane and the kinds that refine it, a bicycle lane or path, a roadway and the kinds that refine it, a shoulder, or an intersection”, which is exactly the set of carriers st.lane_enters admits, so each region argument of the claimed relations has a claimed kind; st.lane_enters is “the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end”, and its clause “it is entry topology: it is decided where the source records it … never inferred from distance, overlap or a road user's velocity” is why approaching is not read from heading or closing speed. dev.stop_sign is the “regulatory sign requiring a full halt”, the sign the words name, and dev.governs, “the travel regions whose traffic the device controls … or an intersection”, ties it to the carrier the vehicle approaches through, as the ontology directs (“the mark that governs that approach is one the source records as marking that carrier”); dev.governs's exclusion “not a stand-in for a position” does not apply, because the place of the halt is read from the crosswalk, the stop line or the view point in s3 and never from where the sign stands. rel.occupies is “a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region”, the anchor that makes the carrier the subject's own."},{"span":"s3","atoms":["st.crosswalk","st.stop_line","st.travel_region","st.entrance_of","st.lane_direction","st.region_geometry","rel.occupies","st.intersection","st.highway","st.on_way","prim.region_offset_along"],"derived":["drv.motion.standstill"],"justification":"“shall stop” is the act: drv.motion.standstill carries the posted definition DEF-NRS-484A-255, “complete cessation from movement”, as a motion state at an observation, with the speed tolerance the sampling leaves to the observer. The first place is the crosswalk “on the near side of the intersection”: st.crosswalk is the “marked crossing, or the unmarked prolongation of sidewalks at an intersection”, and which crossing is the near one is st.entrance_of, “the carrier whose entrance into an intersection a stop line or a crosswalk marks — exactly that carrier's entrance, the line or crossing a vehicle approaching through that carrier halts at or before”, read on the same carrier st.lane_enters relates to the intersection; st.entrance_of's exclusion “not a stand-in for distance to the line” is why nearness never selects the crossing. The second place is st.stop_line, “the transverse line marking where vehicles halt for a device”, taken where the crosswalk's observed list of entrances excludes the carrier, as st.entrance_of's completeness clause permits. The third is the point nearest the intersecting highway, read on the carrier (st.travel_region) against the way the junction lies on: st.highway is “the entire width between the boundary lines of every way”, st.on_way “the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on — … an intersection lies on every way that meets there”, so the intersecting highway is a way the intersection lies on other than the one the carrier lies on. That the halt is at the place and on the near side of it is st.region_geometry, “the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it”, within p.stop_point_tolerance, with the side taken from prim.region_offset_along, “the signed distance … measured along a carrier's designated direction (st.lane_direction)”, whose sign gives the side as the ontology requires (“the side of the mark is read along that carrier's designated direction … never along the road user's heading”); {"concept_id":"drv.interaction.vehicle_file","kind":"formula","contract":"Road user u is one of a file of road users travelling one behind another at the observation: counting u itself, at least the minimum member count of road users have their heading aligned with u's within the same-direction tolerance, lie ahead of or behind u in the same lane, and are within the file reach of u, a distance the caller sets measured between the nearest points of the bodies. lines: {"node_id":"NRS_484A_450_2","law_refs":["NRS-484A-450-2"],"subject":{"binder":"v","class_elements":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"]},"segmentation":[{"id":"s1","text":"Every driver of a vehicle","role":"subject"},{"id":"s2","text":"approaching a stop intersection indicated by a stop sign","role":"trigger"},{"id":"s3","text":"shall stop before entering the crosswalk on the near side of the intersection or, if there is no crosswalk, shall stop at a clearly marked stop line, or if none, then at the point nearest the intersecting highway","role":"obligation"},{"id":"s4","text":"where the driver has a view of approaching traffic on the intersecting highway","role":"standard"},{"id":"s5","text":"before entering the intersection.","role":"condition"}],"elements":[{"span":"s1","atoms":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"],"derived":[],"justification":"“vehicle” is the term DEF-NRS-484A-320 defines and the run admits as the aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, so the span claims ru.aggregate with that id: the atom is “membership of a legal aggregate: the atom's literal argument is an aggregate id”, true where the road user carries an included class, unknown where an included or unresolved class it might carry is unobserved. Its exclusion “not a stand-in for a named road-user class” does not apply, because the admitted aggregate is claimed as the aggregate and never replaced by a class atom; its exclusion of “a relational role such as who drives or controls a vehicle” is respected by reading “driver” through the vehicle's controlled motion (narrowing on this span) rather than as a member of the aggregate."},{"span":"s2","atoms":["st.intersection","st.travel_region","rel.occupies","st.lane_enters","dev.stop_sign","dev.governs"],"derived":[],"justification":"The approach is read as the ontology's section on an act due at a place before an event states it: “a road user's approach to an intersection is a carrier it occupies (rel.occupies) whose entrance end is that intersection”. st.intersection is “the region where two roadways meet, bounded by the prolongation of their edges”, the region the words call the intersection; st.travel_region is the kind the carrier quantifier ranges over, “the union of the kinds a device can govern … a lane and the kinds that refine it, a bicycle lane or path, a roadway and the kinds that refine it, a shoulder, or an intersection”, which is exactly the set of carriers st.lane_enters admits, so each region argument of the claimed relations has a claimed kind; st.lane_enters is “the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end”, and its clause “it is entry topology: it is decided where the source records it … never inferred from distance, overlap or a road user's velocity” is why approaching is not read from heading or closing speed. dev.stop_sign is the “regulatory sign requiring a full halt”, the sign the words name, and dev.governs, “the travel regions whose traffic the device controls … or an intersection”, ties it to the carrier the vehicle approaches through, as the ontology directs (“the mark that governs that approach is one the source records as marking that carrier”); dev.governs's exclusion “not a stand-in for a position” does not apply, because the place of the halt is read from the crosswalk, the stop line or the view point in s3 and never from where the sign stands. rel.occupies is “a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region”, the anchor that makes the carrier the subject's own."},{"span":"s3","atoms":["st.crosswalk","st.stop_line","st.travel_region","st.entrance_of","st.lane_direction","st.region_geometry","rel.occupies","st.intersection","st.highway","st.on_way","prim.region_offset_along"],"derived":["drv.motion.standstill"],"justification":"“shall stop” is the act: drv.motion.standstill carries the posted definition DEF-NRS-484A-255, “complete cessation from movement”, as a motion state at an observation, with the speed tolerance the sampling leaves to the observer. The first place is the crosswalk “on the near side of the intersection”: st.crosswalk is the “marked crossing, or the unmarked prolongation of sidewalks at an intersection”, and which crossing is the near one is st.entrance_of, “the carrier whose entrance into an intersection a stop line or a crosswalk marks — exactly that carrier's entrance, the line or crossing a vehicle approaching through that carrier halts at or before”, read on the same carrier st.lane_enters relates to the intersection; st.entrance_of's exclusion “not a stand-in for distance to the line” is why nearness never selects the crossing. The second place is st.stop_line, “the transverse line marking where vehicles halt for a device”, taken where the crosswalk's observed list of entrances excludes the carrier, as st.entrance_of's completeness clause permits. The third is the point nearest the intersecting highway, read on the carrier (st.travel_region) against the way the junction lies on: st.highway is “the entire width between the boundary lines of every way”, st.on_way “the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on — … an intersection lies on every way that meets there”, so the intersecting highway is a way the intersection lies on other than the one the carrier lies on. {"concept_id":"drv.motion.left_turn","kind":"formula","contract":"The road user has turned to the left: counting from the onset of the turning — the observation at which its rate of change of heading to the left first rose above the onset yaw rate, a rate the caller sets — the heading change accumulated since that onset reaches at least the turn angle, a size the caller sets, to the left. The concept becomes true at the observation at which that angle is first reached, and it holds at the later observations at which the accumulated change still holds that angle, until a later onset starts the count again; the integration is bounded by the heading step, the largest interval between consecutive observations it may integrate across. Where no such onset is observed, with the rate of change of heading known at every observation from the one before it onwards and no interval between consecutive observations longer than the heading step, the concept is unknown and never false, so a turn begun before the recording is never read as one made within it. It states the turning of the body only: no place, no lane, no way and no destination.
